issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->

Automatic JaxPP DualPipeV is now the validated Grug MoE pipeline implementation. The canonical example in #8739 supports explicit 1F1B and zero-bubble references plus automatic ZeroBubble and DualPipeV schedules. Parameters and Adam state are initialized on their owning stages, so the implementation does not materialize the full 67B training state. The root `pipeline` extra installs the pinned JaxPP and CUDA dependencies through the ordinary workspace sync.

The final Snowball 67B-A2B result uses 64 H100s, PP8 x EP8, 16 logical DualPipeV stages, sequence length 8192, batch 256, 32 microbatches, BF16 parameters and compute, and full rematerialization. Median step time is `3.475980327s`, throughput is `603,326.77` tokens/s, median analytic MFU is `19.45529%`, and peak memory is `59,153,094,656` bytes/device. The matched batch-128, 16-microbatch control reaches `543,490.02` tokens/s and `17.52575%` median analytic MFU. Doubling the microbatch count improves median throughput and MFU by `11.01%` with no measured memory increase. Final synthetic-data loss differs by `4.02e-5` between the two runs.

The no-JaxPP baseline uses ordinary Grug training with FSDP8 x EP8 on the same 64 H100s. Batch 256 OOMs before step 0 with a `101.02 GiB` allocation request per device. Batch 64 succeeds at `1.931756s` median step time, `271,404.87` tokens/s, `8.75191%` median analytic MFU, and `29,017,027,044` bytes/device peak. DualPipeV provides `2.223x` the median token throughput and MFU while using `2.039x` the memory. The global batches differ by `4x`, so this comparison measures the viable configurations rather than isolating schedule efficiency at a matched batch.

This meets the practical target for the current work. The measured DualPipeV point is `0.545` percentage point below 20% analytic MFU, and further microbatch scaling is unlikely to justify another 64-H100 experiment without a production workload. The profile attributes the remaining gap primarily to pipeline dependency and SendRecv waiting, especially at the endpoint pair. Attention kernels account for roughly `2.05-4.73%` of exclusive GPU time per physical rank; FSDP and MoE all-gather/reduce-scatter costs are secondary.

Command buffers remain disabled in the validated recipe. JAX 0.11.0 has an XLA mixed-clique initialization bug, while the tested nightly exposes JaxPP DiME multi-communicator initialization and execution deadlocks on the full DualPipeV topology. Deterministic communicator preinitialization fixes the reduced gate but not the full Snowball run. Track that work separately in #7655; it does not block the no-command-buffer result.

PR #8739 is open with all CI checks passing and awaits review. The issue should remain open until that PR lands.

<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

Current baseline

| Area | Current state |
| --- | --- |
| Implementation | Automatic JaxPP DualPipeV in #8739 |
| Model | Snowball 67B-A2B: 67.08B total / about 2.01B active, 26 layers, d2560, 256 experts, top-k 4, sequence 8192 |
| Topology | 64 H100s; PP8 x EP8; 16 logical stages mapped to 8 physical ranks |
| Precision | BF16 parameters, compute, and output; full rematerialization |
| Batch | Global batch 256; 32 microbatches |
| Performance | `3.475980327s` median step; `603,326.77` tokens/s; `19.45529%` median analytic MFU |
| Memory | `59,153,094,656` bytes/device peak |
| No-JaxPP comparison | FSDP8 x EP8 at batch 64: `1.931756s`, `271,404.87` tokens/s, `8.75191%` median analytic MFU, `29,017,027,044` bytes/device peak |
| Runtime caveat | XLA command buffers disabled; follow-up tracked in #7655 |

Decision log

- Use the model-specific Grug implementation as a canonical example that can be adapted to another model. Keep generic mechanics in `levanter.pipeline`; do not hide model partitioning behind a generic high-level pipeline module.
- Use automatic DualPipeV for the validated Snowball recipe. Sixteen logical stages map two stages to each of eight physical pipeline ranks and reduce the warmup/cooldown bubble relative to the eight-stage automatic ZeroBubble schedule.
- Initialize parameters and optimizer state stage-locally. Full-state initialization exceeded H100 memory before pipeline execution.
- Keep the validated 16-stage layer placement. Profiled physical-rank compute differs by up to `1.414x`, but moving one indivisible layer only moves the heavy rank and cannot remove the endpoint bubble.
- Use 32 microbatches for the best measured throughput point. Compared with the matched 16-microbatch control, it improves median throughput and MFU by `11.01%` at identical peak memory.
- Keep command buffers disabled until #7655 has a full-topology fix. Increasing rendezvous timeouts and communicator preinitialization alone did not make the full run execute.
- Treat `19.45529%` as an analytic MFU estimate. The existing FLOP model uses full attention and therefore slightly overestimates work for sliding-window layers.

Prior baseline and negative results

- The earlier explicit-MPMD L24/d2560/e64/top-k4/sequence-4096 result remains a useful historical baseline: `18.2583%` mean MFU and `414,059.10` tokens/s at batch 8192 with 256 microbatches. It is a different model shape and should not be compared directly with the Snowball result.
- Ordinary FSDP8 x EP8 at batch 256 OOMs before step 0 after XLA rematerializes an inefficient batch-to-FSDP reshard and requests `101.02 GiB` per device. Batch 64 fits and reaches `271,404.87` tokens/s and `8.75191%` median analytic MFU with `29.017 GB` peak memory. Its final synthetic-data loss is `0.671852`, within `4.92e-4` of the DualPipeV result.
- Four-stage automatic ZeroBubble works, but eight physical stages with 16 microbatches reached only about `12.83%` mean MFU on the matched Snowball comparison. Long-run DualPipeV reached `16.96%` mean and `17.52%` median MFU at 16 microbatches, a roughly `32%` mean throughput improvement.
- A profile-guided endpoint layer rebalance improved the eight-stage automatic ZeroBubble schedule by only about `1.4%`. The remaining wait is schedule-level.
- Snowball sequence length 32K exceeded memory at PP8. A PP13 experiment was abandoned in favor of validating sequence length 8K.
- Automatic ZeroBubble and explicit 1F1B with command buffers enabled failed during executable initialization on the production JAX pin. The tested JAX nightly passes the reduced XLA initialization gate but deadlocks in JaxPP DiME communicator setup or subsequent execution at full scale.
- Deterministic DiME communicator preinitialization succeeds on a reduced PP8 x EP8 DualPipeV gate. The full Snowball topology still hangs before step 0 with ranks split across runtime compilation, NCCL group completion, and receive waits.
- Attention, Hopper MoE kernels, and intra-stage all-gather/reduce-scatter are not the first optimization target in the representative profile. SendRecv duration is primarily a waiting proxy, not wire-transfer time.

Helpful links

- Implementation PR: #8739
- Command-buffer and DiME follow-up: #7655
- Earlier explicit-MPMD snapshot: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/ecb724da6e
- Earlier explicit baseline: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jaxpp-rno2a-ring-l24-e64k4-b8192-s4096-p4m256-20260711-0107

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: QuACK mismatch is intrinsic approximate SwiGLU, not an adapter bug

- One-H100 exact-shape repro: BF16, 8 experts, H=2560, I=1280, 16 rows/expert, comparing QuACK, Pallas-Triton, and XLA stage by stage.
- W13 is bitwise identical after decoding QuACK's interleaved gated-preactivation layout. W2 is bitwise identical when supplied the same hidden input. Pallas and XLA are bitwise identical end to end.
- QuACK's fused SwiGLU uses fast approximate FP32 `exp2` and reciprocal for sigmoid. From the same preactivation, it differs from JAX SiLU by relative L2 `0.00465063`; final MLP output differs by `0.00519745` relative L2 with `2.5528%` mismatches. The explicit `jaxpp.experimental.mpmd` implementation partitions model weights and optimizer state by stage and runs the requested 24-layer, d2560, sequence-4096 model with GPipe, `std_1f1b`, and queue-correct interleaved GPipe schedules.

The current performance shape uses 64 experts with top-k 4. The best measured point is explicit `std_1f1b`, batch8192/m256, four six-layer stages, ring expert parallelism, CuTe FA4, and eight-warp Pallas-Triton grouped GEMM on RNO2A: mean MFU `18.2583`, p50 `18.3654`, p90 `18.3830`, and `414,059.10` tokens/s. Scaling from m128 to m256 added only `0.1248` mean MFU points, so pipeline occupancy is saturated `1.7417` points below the 20-MFU target.

Profile-guided routing work removed three large rank-2 floating scatter families with explicit Triton kernels and custom VJPs. H100 value/VJP parity and optimized-HLO checks pass, but a pinned 10-step reduced A/B was neutral: bulk ring averaged `9.1735` central MFU versus `9.1595` for `ring_fused`. The backend is not being scaled to L24.

An EP-local QuACK/Sonic grouped-MLP adapter is the first direct expert-kernel result to clear the performance gate: at the exact e64/top-k4/d2560 EP8 microbatch, median forward improves `1.160x` and forward-backward improves `1.108x`. Its approximate fused SwiGLU is now exposed only through explicit research backend `ring_quack_approx`. A paired 10-step one-node training gate stays finite with final relative loss delta `+0.01356%`, while mean MFU improves `4.00%` and median duration falls `4.04%`. The reduced JaxPP gate is next; the 4% whole-step gain alone does not project the current L24 best above 20 MFU.

- FA4 profile: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jaxpp-rno2a-profile-fa4cute-l24-e64k4-b512-s4096-p4m16-20260710-1110

## Current Baseline

| Area | Current state |
| --- | --- |
| Branch | `origin/research/jaxpp-grug-moe` |
| Snapshot | `51eaa57909` (`[docs] Record approximate QuACK training gate`) |
| Model | L24, d2560, 64 experts, top-k 4, sequence 4096, vocab 8192 |
| Pipeline | Explicit MPMD `std_1f1b`, four physical/logical stages, six layers per stage |
| Parallelism | 4x8 H100, expert axis 8, ring EP |
| Kernels | CuTe FA4; Pallas-Triton grouped GEMM, `block_k=32`, 8 warps |
| Best point | batch8192/m256, mean MFU `18.2583` |

## Decision Log

- Use explicit MPMD as the deliverable implementation. Automatic JaxPP remains blocked on non-addressable global-mesh input placement.
- Partition weights and optimizer state before optimizer initialization; this makes the requested 24-layer, 256-expert shape fit.
- Use RNO2A for performance work. Baseline parity and NCCL GDRDMA logs rule out socket fallback.
- Keep four equal six-layer stages and expert axis 8. Tested seven-layer stages and narrower EP do not reach a usable execution point.
- Use 64 experts/top-k 4, CuTe FA4, and eight-warp Pallas-Triton grouped GEMM for the performance boundary.
- Keep ring EP. Ragged all-to-all, DeepEP, Sonic without EP, streamed rings, and owner-local collective-permute combine do not beat it.
- Stop batch scaling at m256; occupancy has saturated around 18.3 MFU.
- Do not scale `ring_fused` to L24; explicit Triton routing is correct but throughput-neutral in the controlled reduced A/B.
- Keep approximate QuACK explicit as `ring_quack_approx`; never change default ring semantics. The finite-step one-node gate passed, but require a reduced JaxPP performance gate before the L24 target.

## Negative Results Index

- Unequal splits with a seven-layer stage OOM or fail to reach execution; six layers per physical stage is the practical limit.
- Expert axis 4 stalls in compilation. Ragged all-to-all reaches only `3.6743` MFU at batch256/m8.
- DeepEP builds and executes its SM90 path but becomes NaN after one finite non-pipelined step.
- Proper Sonic/QuACK without EP reaches `13.9598` MFU; staged weight materialization regresses to `13.8155`.
- Interleaved GPipe hits a compile cliff above the measured m6 point and remains slower than four-stage `std_1f1b`.
- XLA ragged dot regresses to `8.1438` MFU; Triton `block_k=64` regresses to `16.0189`.
- XLA latency-hiding scheduling changes the m128 mean by only `+0.0708` points, below run noise.
- RNO2A cannot create the exportable CUDA VMM allocations needed by zero-copy ragged all-to-all.
- Streamed `ring_ppermute` is numerically unstable and over 1,100x slower on its first timed reduced step.
- Owner-local combine expands to seven collective permutes and does not finish reduced backward compilation.
- Pure-XLA output-oriented combine regresses reduced MFU to `6.2896`; explicit Triton routing restores parity but provides no measurable gain (`9.1595` versus `9.1735`).
- Transfer-priority task construction regresses reduced median MFU by `2.90%` (`8.9006` versus `9.1660`); earlier `mpmd.transfer` calls do not create useful overlap.
- Input-gradient-first backward is gradient-correct and operational but regresses central MFU by `28.75%` (`6.5356` versus `9.1735`); independent block rematerialization overwhelms bubble recovery.
- Exact two-chunk bulk ring passes EP8 output/drop/VJP parity but regresses median forward by `5.30%` and forward-backward by `13.98%`; doubled launches do not hide profitably.

## Current Readout

The implementation milestone is complete. The best observed L24 mean MFU is `18.2583`, and batch/microbatch scaling is saturated. Approximate QuACK improves a one-node L2 whole training step by `4.00%` with a close finite loss trajectory. This is positive but would project to only about `18.99` MFU at L24, so the reduced pipeline gate must show additional benefit before scaling.

## Next Steps

1. Run the pinned reduced L8/b32/m4 explicit-MPMD JaxPP `ring_quack_approx` gate against ring.
2. Scale to L24 only if the reduced pipeline result projects above 20 MFU or combines with another validated improvement that does.
3. Resume automatic JaxPP only after stage-local inputs no longer carry non-addressable global `pipeline` mesh shardings.
4. Keep the self-contained TVM-FFI/QuACK hang reproducer in #7110 ready for human-selected upstream filing.

## Conclusion So Far

Explicit JaxPP MPMD runs the full requested model and sequence shape with stage-partitioned weights and multiple schedules. CuTe FA4 and increased standard-schedule occupancy produced the largest validated gains. The 20-MFU target remains open. Approximate EP-local QuACK is now opt-in and finite-step validated, but its measured `4.00%` whole-step gain is not yet enough to justify the exact L24 run.

Transformer Engine NCCL EP HT remains the ranked follow-up for expert transport.

## Next Steps

1. Implement and run the pinned reduced L8/b32/m4 BF16-versus-FP8 pipeline-wire gate with ring EP.
2. Scale to L24 only if the reduced result credibly projects above 20 MFU.
3. Benchmark Transformer Engine NCCL EP HT non-zero-copy against ring on one H100x8 node before attempting JaxPP integration.
4. Resume automatic JaxPP only after stage-local inputs no longer carry non-addressable global `pipeline` mesh shardings.
5. Keep the self-contained TVM-FFI/QuACK hang reproducer in #7110 ready for human-selected upstream filing.

## Conclusion So Far

Explicit JaxPP MPMD runs the full requested model and sequence shape with stage-partitioned weights and multiple schedules. CuTe FA4 and increased standard-schedule occupancy produced the largest validated gains. The 20-MFU target remains open. Approximate EP-local QuACK is opt-in and finite-step validated but pipeline-neutral; the next gate compresses the exposed inter-stage transfer path itself.

```

</details>

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: r11f isolates an XLA MPMD autotuning deadlock

- All 32 ranks completed JAX and NCCL_EP bootstrap. Stage 0 entered first-forward compilation while stages 1-3 entered JaxPP DIME rendezvous. Native stacks on every stage-0 process converged on `xla::Autotuner::Autotune -> DistributedKeyValueStore::Get`; downstream ranks waited independently for DIME keys. CPU activity was effectively idle.
- OpenXLA defaults `xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=true`. Its config assigner fingerprints the complete HLO module, assigns candidates across every compiler process, and waits for one result key from every process. JaxPP MPMD stages compile different modules, so the expected keys cannot match. r11f was deadlocked, not merely compiling slowly.
- r11f is terminal killed with no live pods and no route fingerprint, `ep_prepare`, loss, or MFU. Its W&B run has no training history: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jaxpp-rno2a-ncclep-routefp-r11f-l8-e64k4-b512-s4096-p4m16-20260724-1221
- The narrow control is now running as r11g parent `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260724-195722`: `--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=false` preserves local online autotuning and disables only cross-process partition/join.
- Automatic standard scheduling also advanced: commit `08f169803e` cleared the non-addressable input `device_put`, then nonconservative loop clustering produced a free task variable. A matched conservative run is capturing the earlier unclustered-equation assertion before testing eager or zero-bubble.
- The accepted `0.2%` ceiling remains scoped to approximate QuACK, NCCL_EP, and FP8 comparisons. Loss/gradient checks stay strict, and exact XLA transport stays bitwise.

Snapshot: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/1939bfeb43

comments.body:
🤖 FP32 reference runs isolate bounded NCCL_EP's remaining numerical miss to token-gradient reduction.

- Token-gradient relative-L2 is `0.290949%`, above the accepted `0.2%` ceiling. Changing the diagnostic from elementwise-mean loss to a token-scaled loss changed absolute magnitude but not relative error.
- FP32 token dispatch generated `payloadu32` forward/backward variants but left token-gradient error unchanged. It remained `1.3288x` faster than the FP32 ring control (`23.4127ms` versus `17.6197ms`).
- r6-r8 all succeeded with eight ranks exit `0`, finite values and gradients, balanced routing, zero drops, and no remaining pods.

This shows the earlier forward and parameter-gradient differences came from production ring's BF16 combine. The residual miss is dispatch-backward reduction order followed by BF16 input-gradient rounding. Under the current ceiling, `nccl_ep_drop` remains blocked from reduced and L24 pipeline runs. Evidence and exact jobs are in [`421a5f6174`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/421a5f6174).

comments.body:
🤖 Update: automatic task ownership fixed; schedule blockers isolated

- Pinned JaxPP deleted `shard_map` equations whose mesh was an `AbstractMesh`, leaving their output variables undefined. Commits [`9e58b5a7c2`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/9e58b5a7c2) and [`66cab1710c`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/66cab1710c) preserve the equation and every automatic task-phase validator now passes. 🤖 Update: compact UB-X slots pass the direct EP8 gate

R14 (`/dlwh/nccl-ubx-direct-ep8-r14-compact-20260727`) ran the target 65,536-row compact receive layout on one H100x8 node. Both balanced and capacity-limited learned-skew routing passed exact map/route/count/drop checks, bitwise dispatch, the `0.002` UB-X-versus-FP32 relative-L2 ceiling, and the `1.10x` transport-speedup floor.

- Balanced: UB-X relative L2 `0.001662022872`; Ring p50 `6.500688076ms`; UB-X p50 `2.048016071ms`; `3.174139191x` speedup.
- Learned skew: accepted/dropped `417371/106917`; UB-X relative L2 `0.001660577729`; Ring p50 `6.604256153ms`; UB-X p50 `1.912575960ms`; `3.453068684x` speedup.
- Learned-skew dispatch storage is `335,544,320` bytes (`320MiB`) per rank, down from R13's `2.5GiB`. Its UB-X p50 improved from `2.295423985ms` to `1.912575960ms`.
- Runtime linkage was NCCL `23007` with exactly one mapped `/tmp/nccl-ubx-db0c814/build/lib/libnccl.so.2.30.7`; UB-X was `0.01`.
- The first task incarnation exited `126` before setup because the synced launcher lacked execute permission. The same Iris job was resubmitted through `bash`; it succeeded and no task remains live.

[`9bb89438dc`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/9bb89438dc) contains the compact direct gate. This admits the layout for the raw JAX FFI test. Expert compute, gradients, JaxPP, and end-to-end MFU remain unmeasured.

Job `/dlwh/jax-ubx-ffi-raw-ep8-r2-20260727` ran pinned NCCL `2.30.7` UB-X through a one-process/eight-device JAX `0.11.0` FFI on one H100x8 node. It completed successfully with no retries or live resources.

- Reduced balanced (`1024` tokens/rank, hidden `256`): bitwise-exact dispatch; relative L2 `0.0016556691`; two-cycle p50 `0.557213ms`.
- Target balanced (`16384` tokens/rank, hidden `2560`): bitwise-exact dispatch; relative L2 `0.0016590385`; two-cycle p50 `7.144761ms`.
- Target learned skew: bitwise-exact dispatch; relative L2 `0.0016589168`; two-cycle p50 `7.060408ms`; accepted/dropped `417371/106917` with drops `[0, 0, 84582, 0, 22335, 0, 0, 0]`.
- Both consecutive cycles passed the user-approved `0.002` ceiling and remained finite.
- Target symmetric memory is `320MiB` per dispatch buffer, `320MiB` per combine buffer, and `1,282MiB` total per GPU.

The timing includes the two transport cycles and the all-gather/FP32 correctness oracle, so it is diagnostic rather than a pure transport comparison. This validates raw JAX integration only. Custom transport VJPs, expert compute, full gradient parity, JaxPP, and end-to-end MFU remain open.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: full UB-X MoE value/VJP passes the fixed numerical gate

Job `/dlwh/jax-ubx-moe-vjp-ep8-r9-20260727` completed on one H100x8 node with exit 0, no retries, and no live task. It used exact Ring routing, compact NCCL 2.30.7 UB-X dispatch/combine, ordinary ragged expert GMM autodiff, FP32 router-weight multiplication in combine backward, and FP32 accepted-route accumulation for the activation-gradient transpose.

- Balanced: `8192/8192` assignments accepted, zero dropped. Relative-L2 was `7.99e-06` output, `4.76e-07` loss, and at most `9.78e-05` across `x`, combine weights, W13, and W2.
- Learned skew: `6530/8192` accepted and `1662` dropped, with exact drops `[0, 0, 1307, 0, 355, 0, 0, 0]`. Relative-L2 was `1.72e-05` output, `8.15e-07` loss, and at most `1.13e-04` across every gradient leaf.
- Every candidate metric passes the unchanged `0.002` ceiling. BF16 Ring remains a diagnostic and differs from the FP32 transport reference by about `0.32-0.56%`, which explains the earlier misleading candidate-versus-Ring failures.
- The reduced gate is latency-bound: UB-X p50 was `0.7694ms` versus Ring `0.5827ms` balanced and `0.7255ms` versus `0.6313ms` learned-skew. This is correctness evidence, not a performance win.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: exact L24 UB-X reproduces the six-layer XLA thunk rendezvous failure

The exact L24/d2560/e64/top-k4/sequence4096 batch8192/m256 EP8 run `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260727-192805` built NCCL 2.30.7 on all four ranks, initialized UB-X at 16,384 local tokens/capacity 65,536, created DIME communicators, and reached six-layer task compilation. This matches the earlier stable/nightly JAX and NCCL 2.28.9/2.30.7 `6,6,6,6` failures, so it is not an UB-X transport, HBM, or numerical result. Commit [`dd0051b84d`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/dd0051b84d) promotes the already validated research control into production explicit MPMD: `GRUG_JAXPP_PRECOMPILE_LOCAL=1` compiles/caches every local task, allocates the receive prologue, synchronizes all ranks, then uses `eval_local_precompiled`. Eleven focused parity tests and changed-file pre-commit including Pyrefly pass.

Next is an L24 `6,6,6,6` UB-X batch512/m16 discriminator with the same microbatch/transport shapes and precompile enabled. A clean compile plus three finite executions is required before retrying exact batch8192/m256. comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: exact UB-X profile recovered and analyzed

- The exact L24/d2560/e64/top-k4/seq4096 batch8192/m256 profile completed, but the original artifact upload used the wrong regional prefix. The trace was salvaged in-region and analyzed by `/dlwh/jaxpp-ubx-profile-analyze-20260727-1432`, which succeeded with exit 0 and left no live failed job.
- The unprofiled exact gate remains `19.8996` mean MFU versus `18.2583` for Ring (+8.99%), missing the `>20` target by 0.50%. The profile run averaged `19.9163` MFU before capture; capture-window overhead lowered it to `19.1937`.
- Device time was 74.57% compute and 25.43% communication. CuTe FA4 forward was the largest kernel at 9.24%. UB-X `CopyAndMaskDispatchKernel` consumed 9.125s across 12,635 calls, averaging 722.2us per 320 MiB output (~465 GB/s). The scalar kernel repeats a 64-bit row division and row-validity load for every BF16 element.
- Send/recv averaged 6.81ms, but the 256.16ms average pre-op gap is upstream pipeline dependency waiting, not evidence of a 2.2 GB/s physical link. Previously tested transfer-priority, input-gradient-first, GPipe, and interleaved schedules remain negative.
- Next: replace the scalar dispatch copy with a row-wise 128-bit copy/mask kernel, require exact routes/counts/drops and relative-L2 <=0.002, run the smallest H100 parity/timing gate, then rerun exact L24 only if the kernel wins.

Links: [artifact](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/artifacts/profiler/jaxpp-rno2a-ubx-profile-l24-e64k4-b8192-s4096-p4m256-precompile-r1-20260727-profiler-salvaged/v0), [XProf](https://iris.oa.dev/proxy/xprof/open?uri=s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxprof%2Fjaxpp-rno2a-ubx-profile-l24-e64k4-b8192-s4096-p4m256-precompile-r1-20260727), [W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jaxpp-rno2a-ubx-profile-l24-e64k4-b8192-s4096-p4m256-precompile-r1-20260727), [logbook commit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/45095e4c5b).

issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This issue defines a 150-run learning-rate and token-budget sweep for the Aug/Hero MoE setup. It covers six model widths from d512 through d2048, five token budgets from 30x through 600x active parameters, and five LR multipliers around the May-Recipe MuonH recommendation. The goal is to see whether the recommended LR remains compute-optimal as both model size and training tokens scale, or whether the Aug/Hero recipe needs a systematic LR adjustment. Current status: the sweep is specified but no runs have been launched yet.

### Helpful links
- `experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/sweep.md` on branch `aug_hero_run_ablations`
- #6711
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Model sizes and architecture are fixed by the hero sweep table (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp/sweep.md`, branch `aug_hero_run_ablations`): d512, d768, d1024, d1280, d1536, d2048, each with its local/global KV split and explicit global-attention layers, a 1024-token sliding window, and sequence length 8192. The `60×` column in that table is the reference token budget; the other multipliers just scale the step count (batch is fixed per size).

## Goal

Map the compute-optimal learning rate relative to the May-Recipe heuristic across model size and token budget — i.e. whether the recommended LR holds, or needs a systematic multiplier, as we scale tokens (30×→600×) and width (d512→d2048).

## Sweep

- **Sizes (6):** d512, d768, d1024, d1280, d1536, d2048.
- **Token budgets (5):** 30×, 60×, 150×, 300×, 600× active params. 60× matches `sweep.md`; steps scale linearly.
- **LR multipliers (5):** 0.7, 0.85, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4 × the recommended MuonH LR.
- **Total: 6 × 5 × 5 = 150 runs.**

### Steps per (size × token budget)

| size | batch | 30× | 60× | 150× | 300× | 600× |
|------|------:|----:|----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| d512  |  32 | 2115 |  4230 | 10575 | 21150 |  42300 |

| d2048 | 512 | 6221 | 12442 | 31106 | 62212 | 124425 |

### Recommended MuonH LR (1.0×) per (size × token budget)

The heuristic LR falls as tokens grow (`adam_lr ∝ tokens^-0.395`), so the base LR is per (size, token budget); each run multiplies its cell by {0.7, 0.85, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4}.

### Naming

`aug-hero-{size}-{mult}x-lr{lrmult}`, e.g. `aug-hero-d1024-150x-lr0.85`.

Defined; **no runs launched.**

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Aug hero LR sweep — results + LR scaling law.** Figures and analysis on branch [`grug-aug-lr-sweep-results`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/grug-aug-lr-sweep-results/experiments/grug/aug_lr_sweep_figs).

## Status: 122/150 cells at full budget

d512–d1536 mostly complete; the remaining ~28 are the largest/longest cells (d2048-300×/600×, d1536-600×), which crash-and-resume off temp checkpoints and are the long pole. Best paloma `macro_loss` per cell (metric used throughout):

| size | 30× | 60× | 150× | 300× | 600× |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d512 | 3.844 | 3.666 | 3.502 | 3.409 | 3.336 |
| d768 | 3.467 | 3.325 | 3.185 | 3.104 | 3.048 |
| d1024 | 3.153 | 3.046 | 2.938 | 2.868 | 2.813 |
| d1280 | 2.994 | 2.899 | 2.802 | 2.740 | 2.692 |
| d1536 | 2.874 | 2.790 | 2.695 | 2.636 | (partial) |
| d2048 | 2.730 | 2.651 | (partial) | (partial) | (partial) |

## Per-cell LR optimum (log-quadratic fit)

Each cell's LR sweep fits a clean parabola in `log(LR)`; the optimum `lr*` **drifts up with token budget** — ~1.0× at 30× to **~1.2–1.4× at 300×/600×** — with a mild downward shift for wider models. The 1.0× heuristic is right for short runs but under-shoots the LR for over-trained budgets.

![per-cell](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/grug-aug-lr-sweep-results/experiments/grug/aug_lr_sweep_figs/lr_sweep_percell_fit_paloma.png?raw=true)

## Learned optimal-LR power law

Fitting the per-cell `lr*` (× the May-Recipe heuristic LR) to `lr = a·tokens^b·hidden^c·batch^0.5` (batch exponent pinned):

```
lr = 34.3 · tokens^-0.346 · hidden^-0.345 · batch^0.5      R² = 0.978, median rel err 1.6%
```

![powerlaw](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/grug-aug-lr-sweep-results/experiments/grug/aug_lr_sweep_figs/lr_powerlaw_fit.png?raw=true)

## Batch-controlled collapse

Dividing out `√batch` (and `hidden^c`) collapses **all 6 model sizes onto a single `tokens^-0.346` line**, R² = 0.979 — the optimal LR is a pure token power law once width and batch are controlled for.

![collapse](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/grug-aug-lr-sweep-results/experiments/grug/aug_lr_sweep_figs/lr_batch_collapse.png?raw=true)

## vs. current heuristic, and at the d6144 / 15T target

muonh LR = `coeff·tokens^p·hidden^q·batch^0.5` (seq 8192 folded into coeff):

| | coeff | tokens exp | hidden exp |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ours (fit)** | 34.35 | **−0.346** | **−0.345** |
| **current heuristic** | 25.89 | −0.395 | −0.150 |

Two structural disagreements: ours decays **slower with tokens** (wants more LR at large budgets) and **much faster with width**. At **d6144 / 15T tokens** these nearly cancel — our law prescribes **~1.07× the heuristic's LR** (batch-independent; e.g. batch 4096 → heuristic 2.80e-3 vs ours 2.99e-3).

**Caveat:** that agreement is a coincidental cancellation, and d6144/15T is a large extrapolation — width is **3× beyond** the widest swept model (d2048) and 15T is well past the 600× budget. The `hidden^-0.345` term (the biggest disagreement) is the least-constrained; a d6144-or-wider point is needed to pin it before trusting either law at 15T.

issues.author: claude[bot]
issues.body:
The TPU canary ferry (Grug MoE smoke test) crashes at compile time on the first `train_step`. On this run the crash was deterministic across all 4 task attempts, so `max_task_failures` was exceeded and the job failed.

The expert grouped-matmul fails to lower on TPU v6e: the megablox GMM `pallas_call` builds an output `BlockSpec((512, 32))` for an output array of shape `(524288, 128)`. Pallas requires the last block dim to be divisible by 128 or equal to the array dim; 32 is neither.

```
ValueError: The Pallas TPU lowering currently requires that the last two
dimensions of your block shape are divisible by 8 and 128 respectively, or be
equal to the respective dimensions of the overall array. Block spec for outputs
in pallas_call kernel at .../pallas/ops/tpu/megablox/gmm.py:393 has block shape
(Blocked(block_size=512), Blocked(block_size=32)), array shape (524288, 128)
```

Call path: `levanter/grug/_moe/scatter.py:48` (expert MLP projection), then `haliax.nn.ragged_dot._ragged_dot_megablox_impl` (`lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py:93`), then `jax.experimental.pallas.ops.tpu.megablox.gmm`. The output n=128 equals the canary model intermediate_dim.

Reproduce:
1. Run the TPU canary ferry `python -m experiments.ferries.canary_ferry` on `v6e-4` (`CANARY_MODEL`: hidden_dim=32, intermediate_dim=128, num_experts=32, num_experts_per_token=2, num_layers=4).
2. The failure is intermittent across scheduled runs (history below); it reproduces when the megablox GMM lowers fresh instead of loading from the shared JAX compilation cache.

Expected: the megablox GMM lowers with a valid output block (last dim divisible by 128, or equal to n) and the canary trains to the regression gate.

<details><summary>Root-cause status (unresolved discrepancy)</summary>

The observed tn=32 does not match the checked-out tiling logic. `_megablox_tile_size()` at HEAD returns an n-tile of 1024, so `_ragged_dot_megablox_impl` passes `tiling[2] = min(n=128, 1024) = 128`, which would produce a valid `(512, 128)` output block. Static reading of the current code does not explain how tn=32 was emitted. This gap is the crux and needs a kernel owner.

The invalid Megablox grouped-matmul output block is produced in the left-hand-side gradient path. issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
Builds of the patched PJRT wheel in `marin-community/xla` cache `~/.cache/bazel` wholesale, about 11.6 GB against GitHub's documented 10 GB per-repository limit. Retention is unpredictable, and the difference is 1m35s of build time versus 3h31m.

| run | restore | build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [33013385685](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/actions/runs/33013385685) | 3m38s | 1m35s |
| [33093433428](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/actions/runs/33093433428) | 0s, nothing to restore | 3h31m33s |

A save at 2026-08-26T21:12Z was gone by the next build at 2026-08-27T16:29Z, which then paid a full cold compile. A save at 2026-08-27T20:04Z is still present a day later. Both entries are the same size, so exceeding the cap does not by itself explain which one survives.

The cached directory holds more than compile output. `external/` and `cache/repos/` carry fetched repositories including the CUDA 13 redistributables, which cost minutes to download again, while `execroot/.../bazel-out` carries the object files that cost hours to rebuild. No size breakdown has been taken, so which part dominates the 11.6 GB is unknown, and that is the first thing needed.

Impact is bounded. Builds run only on pushes to `main` that touch the wheel, so this costs 3½ hours on a refresh or a build-script change, not on routine work. Promotion runs from a published candidate and never compiles.

Done when:

- a size breakdown of the bazel output base is recorded from a build that runs anyway
- the cached content is small enough to be retained between consecutive builds
- two consecutive builds restore the cache, and the second compiles in minutes rather than hours

issues.author: WingchunSiu
issues.body:
Human tl;dr: an experiment to understand teacher-student interaction in agentic SFT through the student's own rank/surprisal statistics over traces.

## TL;DR

Proposal. In reasoning-CoT distillation the teacher paradox is documented and measurable: stronger teachers do not reliably produce better students, and the Rank-Surprisal Ratio (RSR, [arXiv 2601.14249](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14249)), a student-relative trace score, predicts post-training reasoning performance (Spearman ~0.86, 5 students × 11 teachers). Agentic SFT shows the same paradox but has no equivalent measurement, and agentic traces differ in ways that could break the result: environment-produced tokens interleave with assistant actions, and trajectories end in verifiable outcomes. This experiment tests whether the conclusion transfers: score traces under the pre-SFT student, then check whether the score orders traces by downstream SFT utility, first against already-trained arms with known eval outcomes, then by training on top / mid / bottom-scoring slices of one pool and comparing held-out eval. Per-teacher score aggregates would then give a pre-SFT estimate of teacher fit.

## Motivation

The RSR paper established the reasoning case: likelihood-only suitability metrics favor traces the student already reproduces, while effective traces combine low absolute probability with relatively high-ranked tokens under the student. The mechanism should generalize: SFT moves the student's distribution toward the data, so a trace's teaching value depends on where it sits relative to that distribution. Traces the student already reproduces carry no signal; traces far outside its reach are memorized, not learned; in between is a "just about right" zone where learning should be most productive.

Two per-action statistics locate a trace in this picture. Surprisal (negative log probability of the observed action) measures how unexpected an action is. Rank (where the action falls among the student's own candidates) measures whether it was reachable at all: rank 3 means nearly produced, rank 5000 means effectively unreachable. Rank is robust to trace length and probability scale; surprisal keeps the magnitude information rank discards. Both cost one forward pass per token. (Scoring covers assistant tokens only, matching the standard SFT mask.)

Falsifiable predictions:

1. Arm ordering discriminates two sweet-spot geometries. If the metric transfers as constructed, utility improves monotonically as RSR decreases (the paper's direction). If the sweet spot sits in score space for agentic traces, mid-score traces win. Top / mid / bottom / random arms separate the two.
2. The zone moves with student strength: the same teacher trace shifts from "just right" to "unreachable" as the student weakens. If true, this explains teacher × student interactions mechanistically, and per-teacher aggregates become an interpretability read on teacher fit.
3. The score must beat free baselines (verifier outcome, pass rate, mean NLL) to be worth anything.

## Hypothesis or Goal

- H1 (explanation): the scores predict SFT utility beyond task mix, length, token budget, outcome, and mean NLL.
- H2 (sampling): score-selected traces improve held-out agentic performance over task-mix- and supervised-token-matched controls.

Non-goal: re-establishing the teacher paradox itself. The paradox is the premise; the claim is that its student-relative origin is measurable before training, and actionable for selection.

## Design

The variable under test is the individual trace. Two stages:

- Stage 1, retrospective, no training. Score public trace datasets and check whether dataset-level score rankings match the known outcomes of already-trained arms. Primary material: the Qwen3-8B ablation farm behind the OpenThoughts-Agent paper (~40 checkpoints trained from the same Qwen3-8B student; per-arm OT-TBLite / SWE-V-100 / TB2.0 scores in [arXiv 2606.24855](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24855)). Secondary: the OpenThinkerAgent-32B data-scale ladder (six nested arms) and the #8225 Snowball stage-3 arms (a cross-recipe and cross-student-strength check). Predictions are written down before outcomes are inspected. The scorer is always the student that was (or will be) trained, because the claim is student-relative.
- Stage 2, prospective, within-task. Roll k independent traces per task from a fixed teacher on training-side task sets (disjoint from the eval suite), with verifier rewards recorded. Arms: top / mid / bottom / random by score within each task, so task mix is identical across arms by construction, plus outcome-only and pass-rate controls. Small LoRA probes test arm separation; full SFT runs are decision-grade. Paired held-out eval under the canonical policy (#7958); a difference is clear when the paired task-level 95% interval excludes zero (#8483).

Out of scope: task-level selection. Trace scores aggregate to task/source rankings for free and may be reported as descriptive byproducts, but nothing here proposes removing tasks or sources from any mix.

## Status

Proposal. Batch scoring and paired-eval tooling are implemented; nothing above is blocked on new infrastructure. Public trace pools are effectively one-trace-per-task (e.g. DCAgent/nl2bash-32ep rows are sequential segments of single trials, not i.i.d. resamples), so the within-task claim requires Stage 2's self-generation. Stage 1 material is fully public.

## Links

- Predecessor metric (reasoning CoT): [Rank-Surprisal Ratio, arXiv 2601.14249](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14249)
- OpenThoughts-Agent paper (Qwen3-8B ablation farm): [arXiv 2606.24855](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24855)
- Trace dataset registry: #6191
- Cold-start SFT reference arms: #8225
- Canonical eval policy: #7958
- Per-trace rewards for overlapping sources: [open-thoughts/AgentTrove](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/AgentTrove)

## Asks

1. Is the design sound? Control arms and eval criteria especially: what would you change before spending compute on it?
2. Pointers to anything worth knowing first: related efforts, prior failures, eval pitfalls.

comments.author: AbarnaaSree
comments.body:
This looks like a strong design. One thing I’d add before spending on Stage 2 is a leakage/sensitivity check around trace length and task difficulty, since both could correlate with rank/surprisal and downstream utility. I’d also report the score distribution and correlation with verifier outcome and mean NLL separately, so it’s clear whether RSR adds predictive value beyond those baselines.

For the prospective arms, keeping top/mid/bottom selection strictly within each task as proposed seems important. I’d also consider fixing the selection quantiles and evaluating the same trace set across multiple seeds to distinguish a real score effect from sampling variance.

The nightly Grug multislice smoke failed because the **second TPU slice never provisioned**: GCP had **no `v6e-8` capacity in `us-east5-b`**, so the autoscaler could not bring up slice index 1. Slice 0 came up, entered Levanter's Megascale (multislice) init, and waited the full **3600 s** for its peer before raising `TimeoutError`. That surfaced up the stack as `RuntimeError: 1 step(s) failed`.

This is an **infra/scheduling (capacity)** failure, not a training or controller bug. The run needs 2 x `v6e-8` slices (`GRUG_MULTISLICE_SLICE_COUNT=2`); only one was schedulable.

## Root cause chain

1. Parent training job `.../grug-train-grug-multislice-smoke-29742549799-1` requests 2 tasks (one per `v6e-8` slice).
2. Task/slice **0** booted and ran `experiments/grug/base/train.py -> trainer.initialize() -> configure_megascale_from_iris()`, which blocks until **all** Iris tasks register. Its log repeats for ~1 h:
   `levanter.megascale Waiting for Iris tasks before Megascale init; missing task indexes: [1]`
3. Task/slice **1** never started (per-task summary shows `DURATION -`, no container ran). The autoscaler repeatedly failed to create its slice:
   `Bootstrap failed for slice marin-tpu-v6e-preemptible-8-us-east5-b-... : There is no more capacity in the zone "us-east5-b" [EID: 0x4a60382432847277]`
4. After 3600 s, slice 0 raised `TimeoutError: Timed out after 3600.0s waiting for all Iris tasks before Megascale init` -> `RuntimeError: 1 step(s) failed`; job marked `failed`.

Training never started (no optimizer step ran), so there is no metric regression and almost certainly no W&B step data for this run.

## Not reproducible locally

Zonal preemptible-TPU capacity is a live GCP condition; there is nothing to reproduce in code. The failure is environmental (no `v6e-8` in `us-east5-b` at run time), amplified by the fact that a partial multislice acquisition (1 of 2 slices) blocks for the full 3600 s before failing.

- **Fail fast on unsatisfiable multislice:** slice 0 held a `v6e-8` for ~1 h while its peer was already known-unschedulable. Megascale init (or the Iris coscheduler) could abort early when a sibling slice's scale-group has entered a terminal `slice_failed`/no-capacity state, instead of waiting the full `timeout`.

- **Retry/backoff:** a scheduled retry on transient zonal exhaustion would likely have passed.

Job: /runner/iris-run-job-20260829-151124/grug-train-grug-multislice-smoke-33259534576-1
State: running  exit=0  failures=1  preemptions=1
Tasks: 0/2 completed  pending=1  running=1
  TASK  STATE    EXIT  DURATION         DIAGNOSTIC
     0  running  -     51m (attempt 2)  Exit code: 1. stderr: TimeoutError: Timed out after 3600.0s waiting for all Iris tasks before Megascale init
     1  pending  -     -
```

Evidence (controller-log window ~17:16–17:27 UTC):

- Slice 1's `v6e-8` never came up. The one `tpu_v6e-preemptible_8-us-east5-b` slice in the window bootstrap-failed: `marin-tpu-v6e-preemptible-8-us-east5-b-20260829-1718-c5d90539` → `There is no more capacity in the zone "us-east5-b" [EID: 0xbff77f23135115a1]`, `n_registered=0`.
- `us-east5-b` stockout in the (short) captured window: **3** `v6e-8` + **15** `v6e-4` `no more capacity` lines. Autoscaler for `tpu_v6e-preemptible_8-us-east5-b` held at `demand=1, total=1, pending=0` — it never sustained a second slice.
- Training never started (no optimizer step), so no W&B step metrics for this run.

Because slice 0 *did* acquire and then held a `v6e-8` for 2h+ across two 3600 s waits while its peer was already known-unschedulable, the **"fail fast on partial multislice acquisition"** follow-up from the original report *would* have helped this run — alongside the **multi-zone/region fallback** and **retry-on-transient-stockout** follow-ups.

## Canary run context

|---|---|
| Lane | `grug-multislice` (GCP / TPU) |
| Job ID | `/runner/iris-run-job-20260829-151124` |
| Training subjob | `.../grug-train-grug-multislice-smoke-33259534576-1` (task 0 running/looping, task 1 pending) |
| Config | 2 × `v6e-8`, region `us-east5`, batch 32, 5 steps |
| GHA run | https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33259534576 |
