issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

A JAX-Toolbox-derived Iris task image can run the exact #7507 full-MoE workload on 64 GB200 GPUs, so the preserved-package task-image contract is viable for optional GB200 rollout. The scanned comparison measured 25.5954% median MFU, a 0.505% time-adjusted regression against the two current-image controls; that passes the proposed 2% adoption gate but gives no performance reason to switch by default. The full 48-layer model remains unusable without `jax.lax.scan`: independently initialized layers requested a 905.27 GiB temporary arena before step 0, and explicit block-boundary optimization barriers changed the request by only 128 KiB. These no-scan probes avoided the historical null-module CUBIN signature, but they hit an earlier OOM boundary and therefore do not prove that Toolbox fixes CUBIN loading in general.

### Helpful links
- [Design PR #7524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7524)
- [Research logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260722-fix-7507/.agents/logbooks/jax_toolbox_7507.md)
- [Scanned Toolbox W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jax-toolbox-7507-toolbox-scan-c-20260722-1523)
- [No-scan barrier W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jax-toolbox-7507-toolbox-noscan-barrier-a-20260722-1837)
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Goal

Define the task-image contract needed to use NVIDIA JAX-Toolbox on `cw-us-east-08a`, then compare its MFU and no-scan compiler behavior against the current Iris GPU image on the exact #7507 model.

## Results

The single-node canary confirmed ARM64 support and four visible GB200 devices. The production prototype derives an Iris task image from an immutable Toolbox digest and uses `/etc/iris/preserved-python-packages` to keep the image-owned JAX/CUDA stack outside the workspace overlay.

The exact control → Toolbox → control sequence completed on 16 four-GPU GB200 hosts per run. Medians over steps 5–11 and 15–19 were:

| Image | Seconds/step | Tokens/second | MFU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [Control A](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jax-toolbox-7507-control-scan-a-20260722-195616) | 14.6695 | 285,920.95 | 25.8327% |
| [Toolbox](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jax-toolbox-7507-toolbox-scan-c-20260722-1523) | 14.8055 | 283,293.64 | 25.5954% |
| [Control B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jax-toolbox-7507-control-scan-b-20260722-1539) | 14.7376 | 284,600.13 | 25.7134% |

Control drift was 0.462%. Linear interpolation at the treatment timestamp estimates a 0.505% Toolbox regression in throughput and MFU.

The corrected no-scan run initialized a tuple of independent layer modules and retained per-layer rematerialization. It failed before step 0 on a 972,028,334,224-byte allocation. A second run inserted optimization barriers between all 48 blocks and requested 972,028,203,152 bytes, only 131,072 bytes less. Both requests were 905.27 GiB against a 138.22 GiB allocator limit. [No-barrier run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jax-toolbox-7507-toolbox-noscan-modules-a-20260722-1640), [barrier run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/jax-toolbox-7507-toolbox-noscan-barrier-a-20260722-1837).

## Decision log

- Target an Iris GPU base image derived from a pinned JAX-Toolbox digest; do not preinstall Marin, Levanter, or Haliax.
- Synchronize workspace packages at task startup while preserving image-owned distributions named in `/etc/iris/preserved-python-packages`.
- Keep task-image selection explicit during rollout so PyTorch and vLLM jobs retain their current images.
- Accept the Toolbox scanned performance result against a 2% gate; the measured direction is a small regression.
- Stop the explicit-barrier line of investigation. Per-layer checkpointing already inserts optimization barriers, and the additional barriers changed the arena by only 128 KiB.

## Links

- [Design PR #7524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7524)
- [Research logbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260722-fix-7507/.agents/logbooks/jax_toolbox_7507.md)
- [JAX-Toolbox](https://github.com/NVIDIA/JAX-Toolbox)
- [GB200 cluster config](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/config/cw-us-east-08a.yaml)

## Conclusion

JAX-Toolbox is viable as an optional Iris GB200 task image under the proposed preserved-package contract. It is 0.505% slower than the time-adjusted current-image control on #7507. It avoids the known CUBIN signature in the tested no-scan compilations, but XLA instead plans a 905.27 GiB arena. Additional block-boundary optimization barriers are redundant with the barriers already introduced by per-layer checkpointing and do not reduce that arena.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Correction to the no-scan result above: withdraw the conclusion that the 863.96 GiB failure characterizes a true unstacked model.

`SCALE_SCAN_LAYERS=0` changed execution to a Python loop, but `Transformer.init` still created one `ArrayStacked[Block]`. The loop iterated over `ArrayStacked.unstacked()` views instead of independently initialized layer-module pytrees. Per-layer rematerialization was enabled, but the parameter representation remained stacked.

Commit [`09b2054d8e`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/09b2054d8e) now selects the representation during initialization: `ArrayStacked[Block]` for `lax.scan`, and a tuple of independent `Block` modules for no-scan. The two representations produce identical logits in the local parity test.

The corrected exact 64-GPU Toolbox run is `/dlwh/jax-toolbox-7507-toolbox-noscan-modules-a-20260722-1640-coord`. Until it terminates, the earlier OOM should not be used to judge true no-scan viability or CUBIN behavior.

🤖 The corrected true no-scan probe is complete. Commit `09b2054d8e` initializes a tuple of independent `Block` modules when `scan_layers=false` and keeps per-layer rematerialization; a CPU parity test produces identical logits to the scanned representation from the same initialization key.

The exact #7507 shape then ran on 16 four-GPU GB200 hosts with the Toolbox image. The first `jit_train_step` compiled for about 26 minutes and failed before step 0 when CUDA requested 972,028,334,224 bytes (905.27 GiB) against a 138.22 GiB allocator limit. There were no retries, preemptions, MFU samples, null-module loads, or in-memory-CUBIN errors.

This supersedes the earlier 863.96 GiB stacked-view result. Independently initialized modules preserve the same computation but make the unrolled temporary-arena problem slightly larger. 🤖 Block-boundary optimization barriers do not reduce the true no-scan arena.

Commit `239b663c4d` inserted `jax.lax.optimization_barrier` between all 48 independently initialized blocks. The exact 64-GPU Toolbox run failed before step 0 after 26m37s. Its allocation request was 972,028,203,152 bytes, versus 972,028,334,224 bytes without barriers: a reduction of 131,072 bytes, or about 0.0000135%.

issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
Imagine the following situation: someone running on interactive queue requests a v4-16 and at the time of their request, this is schedulable. Then, someone running on the production queue requests a v4-8 but we are now at capacity.

In an ideal world, where the slices were fungible, we'd want to preempt the interactive queue job, kill the v4-16, and spin up a v4-8 to serve the production user. 

On our spot/preemptible capacity, we don't do this because there is no guarantee that killing the v4-16 will allow us to spin up the v4-8.

However, on our limited reserved capacity we can guarantee this since the compute is fungible up to our cap.

As such, specifically for the reserved compute, we should preempt lower priority jobs to serve higher priority jobs even if the chip types dont match.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue and walk the Iris scheduler preemption code
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (none found; #6086 covers unrelated reconcile findings)
- [x] Decide scope — design change, too large for an agent PR
- [x] Post research + proposed approach for human review

# Research

Today's preemption pass hard-gates victims by `device_variant`. Solo preemptors only evict solo victims of the same variant ([`scheduling_policy.py#L560`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling_policy.py#L560)); coscheduled preemptors only evict a whole slice of the same variant whose member count ≥ preemptor's ([`scheduling_policy.py#L622-L628`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling_policy.py#L622-L628)). Neither path knows whether the victim's worker is on reserved vs preemptible/on-demand capacity — `RunningTaskInfo` carries `device_variant` but no `capacity_type` ([`scheduling_policy.py#L94-L111`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling_policy.py#L94-L111)), and the `preemptible` worker attribute lives on `WorkerCapacity.attributes` but isn't read in the preemption pass.

The same-variant gate is correct on spot/preemptible — eviction frees a fixed slice shape the autoscaler can't reshape on demand. On reserved capacity it's over-conservative for the reason in the issue: chips are fungible up to cap.

**Relevant code**
- [`scheduling_policy.py#L538-L592`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling_policy.py#L538-L592) — `_preempt_solo` same-variant gate
- [`scheduling_policy.py#L595-L638`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling_policy.py#L595-L638) — `_preempt_coscheduled` variant + slice-shape gate
- [`scheduling_policy.py#L476-L535`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/scheduling_policy.py#L476-L535) — `get_running_tasks_with_band_and_value` (RunningTaskInfo source; no capacity_type)
- [`constraints.py#L1147-L1154`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/constraints.py#L1147-L1154) — `preemptible` attribute injection from `capacity_type`
- [`autoscaler/routing.py#L232`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/autoscaler/routing.py#L232) — autoscaler routes demand per scale group's `capacity_type`

# Proposed approach (design change — needs human review before PR)

1. Plumb `capacity_type` (or just `is_reserved`) onto `RunningTaskInfo` by reading `WellKnownAttribute.PREEMPTIBLE` (and capacity_type if available) from the worker attributes already in the scheduling snapshot. Symmetrically tag each `PreemptionCandidate` with whether the preemptor is targeting reserved (it already constrains via `preemptible_constraint`, so this is mostly extracting the existing constraint).
2. Relax the variant gate in `_preempt_solo` and `_preempt_coscheduled` to: `wanted_variant == victim_variant` OR `preemptor_targets_reserved AND victim_on_reserved AND same_reserved_pool`. The hypothetical-capacity check stays — solo cross-variant preemption only works if the freed worker can actually host the request post-eviction (mostly meaningful for CPU/RAM-bound bin packing; TPU slices are whole-worker-owned and need pool reshaping).
3. Coscheduled cross-variant is the harder case: a v4-8 preemptor evicting a v4-16 slice can't land this tick because TPU shape is a property of the physical slice, not the worker. The realistic plan is "evict now, autoscaler reshapes the reserved pool, preemptor lands next tick" — i.e. relax the gate and rely on the autoscaler/provider to serve the new shape from freed reserved cap.

# Open design questions (block implementation)

- **Granularity of "reserved pool"**: is fungibility "all reserved scale groups" or "within one scale group"? Scale-group routing today is per-group ([`autoscaler/routing.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/autoscaler/routing.py)), and a v4 reservation isn't fungible with a v5p one — needs an explicit "reserved-pool key" (region + family + cap-pool id?) carried on workers and on the preemptor's matching worker set.
- **Thrash safety**: today eviction credit is computed against `WorkerCapacity` deltas. If we evict a v4-16 and the provider can't actually re-provision a v4-8 (cap already claimed by other reservations, regional shortage), we kill an interactive job for nothing and the preemptor re-fires next tick. Gate the cross-variant eviction on a dry-run autoscaler-can-serve check, or add a per-victim cooldown.
- **Scope of relaxation**: does cross-variant apply only when the preemptor is PRODUCTION evicting INTERACTIVE/BATCH, or also INTERACTIVE→BATCH? The issue's example is PRODUCTION→INTERACTIVE; I'd start there.

# Sizing

Implementation is ~200–400 LOC plus tests, plus a short design doc in `.agents/projects/` covering the three questions above. Not a self-contained agent fix — flagging for human review.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
An 8-task coscheduled SkyRL job on cw-rno2a entered an unrecoverable state after a preemption (`/power/curriculum-rl-r2-full/users-power-checkpoints-curriculum-rl-naive-dapo-2026.08.29.20-da4144a5bf73`). Task 0 (Ray head/trainer entrypoint) was preempted; worker tasks 1–6 exited 0 when the head disappeared and were marked terminally `succeeded`; tasks 0 and 7 reverted to `pending`. On reschedule the new head waits for 7 Ray workers but only task 7 can ever rejoin, so the job blocks at placement-group creation indefinitely while holding 2 nodes, and the job-level state stays `running`.

Reproduce:
1. Run a multi-node coscheduled Ray job at a preemptible priority.
2. Preempt the head task while workers are alive; workers exit 0 and go terminal-succeeded.
3. The retried head waits forever for a worker gang that cannot reform.

Expected: preemption of any member of a coscheduled group restarts the whole gang — a worker's exit status is meaningless once the head is gone. Complementarily, jobs of this shape should support leader-determined completion: task 0's outcome defines the job, and sibling tasks are auxiliary (restarted with the leader, terminated when the leader finishes) rather than carrying independent terminal success states.

Done when:
A preempted head task reschedules with its full worker gang re-formed (no permanently succeeded siblings), or job configuration allows declaring task 0 the leader whose outcome governs the group's lifecycle.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Research

[`apply_one_transition`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py) records exit 0 as terminal `SUCCEEDED` and triggers coscheduled peer cascades only for failure states. [`find_coscheduled_siblings`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/peers.py) reads active tasks only, so a SkyRL worker that exits 0 after head loss is absent from the later retry cascade. The [pinned MarinSkyRL launcher](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/c6ec7e2de67fb2cf28a6310d8ad863782cae85d4/cloud/iris/iris_backend.py) already submits multi-node GPU runs with Iris replicas and coscheduling.

Proposed Fix

When a coscheduled member retries after failure or preemption, return active and already-succeeded siblings to `PENDING`. Preserve each succeeded attempt in attempt history and leave sibling retry counters unchanged. Add a deterministic controller journey for succeeded workers followed by a retriable head preemption, then verify that all tasks launch a second attempt together.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 Fix is open in #8775. Retriable failure or preemption now returns every coscheduled Task to pending, including siblings whose prior Attempts succeeded, so the whole gang can reschedule. Successful Attempts remain immutable and retry counters stay unchanged. The regression covers succeeded sibling tasks followed by head-task preemption; the focused coscheduling suite and full Iris suite pass locally. Marin’s pinned SkyRL launcher already opts multi-node jobs into Iris coscheduling.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 A second, adjacent failure mode from the same incident: after the wedged job was cancelled (`Terminated by user`), the submitting driver's log-streaming step (`[rl-iris] Now streaming logs ... This process runs until the job ends.`) never observed the kill and blocked indefinitely, holding the step's executor lock. A successor driver polling that lock could not take over until the wedged driver was itself killed. Kill/cancel of a child job should be terminal for the parent's streaming wait, the same as failure. Worth covering in the same fix or a sibling PR.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body: Forwarding servers don't serve any queries, so the index building and remote object backups are unnecessary. They should simply collect and forward logs from their locally compacted segments.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Locate Finelog forwarding-server code and index/backup logic
- [x] Determine root cause and scope
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no overlapping PR; #8748 is adjacent object-storage work)
- [x] Post analysis — **out of PR scope: design change, needs human review**

---

**Research**

Forwarding servers are ordinary `Live` stores that additionally spawn a `Forwarder`; the store itself has no notion of a forwarding-only role, so per-namespace maintenance runs the full `flush → compact → sync → evict → index-backfill` cycle regardless ([`run_maintenance`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/namespace.rs#L1934-L2015)). Index building is gated only by the static per-namespace policy [`segment_indexes_enabled_for`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/rust/src/policies.rs#L164-L167), which is identical on hub and regional servers — there is no server-role input to turn it off for a forwarder. Remote backup is [`sync_step`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/namespace.rs#L1512), uploading L≥1 segments to the object store.

The blocker is that remote backup is load-bearing for **retention**, not just durability. Eviction reclaims only `BOTH` (local+remote) segments via `select_eviction_candidate`, and [`evict_segment`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/namespace.rs#L1644-L1679) refuses to destroy `LOCAL`-only data — the test `eviction_skips_local_only_when_no_remote` (namespace.rs:3987) asserts local-only segments are never evicted. So dropping backup on a forwarder as configured today grows local disk without bound; there is no size/age reclamation path for local-only segments.

**Proposed approach (for review — not implementing as a PR)**

Doing this safely is three coupled changes, not a two-line gate, so it exceeds the self-contained-bugfix bar:

1. **Server-role signal.** Thread a forwarding-only flag from the CLI (`args.forwarding` non-empty, already parsed in [main.rs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/rust/src/main.rs#L303)) through `Store::new*` into each `Namespace`, rather than deriving indexing from the global static policy. Decide whether this is a new `ServeMode` variant (`Forward`) or an orthogonal boolean — `ServeMode` currently means "what a process may touch," and forward-only fits that framing.
2. **Gate the two steps.** Skip `sync_step` and index backfill in `run_maintenance` when forwarding-only (leaving `cleanup_disabled_index_bundles` to remove stale bundles on a converted server).
3. **Retention for local-only segments.** Since the hub becomes the durable archive for forwarded rows, a forwarding-only store must treat local segments as ephemeral scratch and evict `LOCAL`-only segments by size/age. This is a new eviction path; the forwarder is already best-effort and tolerates eviction removing un-forwarded segments ([forwarding.rs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/rust/src/server/forwarding.rs#L27-L44)), so at-least-once semantics hold, but the "evict rows that never forwarded" behavior is a policy decision worth an explicit sign-off.

Open questions for a maintainer: (a) is a forwarding server ever queried locally as a fallback (the forwarder docstring calls the local store "the system of record")? If yes, dropping indexes/backup changes that guarantee. (b) Should local-only eviction wait on the forward cursor, or stay purely size/age-bounded? Deploy wiring in [`config.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/src/finelog/deploy/config.py#L219-L241) (forwarders currently also set `remote_log_dir`) would follow whichever shape is chosen.

## Summary

This tracker keeps the dense Qwen3-8B TPU inference parity matrix readable and current for Levanter versus vLLM-TPU. The matrix is meant to report separate regime rows instead of a single average, covering decode-heavy, mixed, prefill-heavy, pressure, churn, sampled `n=4`, greedy `n=1`, and longer output cases with throughput, token-completion, admission, and timing fields. Current anchors show Levanter close on v6e decode-heavy (`0.938` decode tok/s ratio), below target on v6e mixed (`0.819`), still below target on v6e prefill-heavy after corrected and post-split reruns (`0.742` to `0.758`), and substantially behind on the bounded v5p TP=4 mixed row (`0.600`). The current recommendation is to avoid automatic matrix reruns from this tracker: after PR #6185 lands or maintainers explicitly authorize reruns from that head, refresh the highest-value v6e decode-heavy and corrected mixed rows first; do not spend more runs on the prefill-heavy row unless #6229 chooses another optimization experiment, and treat v5p follow-up as a throughput-gap investigation tracked by #6230.

### Helpful links
- Parent rollout epic: #6227
- Dense matrix harness PR: #6176
- Admission/timing fields PR: #6185
- Prefill-heavy follow-up: #6229
- v5p follow-up: #6230
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description
Finish and maintain the dense Qwen3-8B TPU inference parity matrix for Levanter versus vLLM-TPU. Report results by regime instead of collapsing them into one average: greedy `n=1`, sampled `n=4`, `o128`, `o512`, likely `o2048`, logprobs on/off, decode-heavy, mixed, prefill-heavy, pressure, and churn cases.

PR #6176 (`codex/qwen3-dense-parity-matrix`, head `104bf901e33c5f0b34d32d4f59edf27b82f66714`) carries the dense matrix harness/config and has all visible checks green. PR #6185 head `f55913d1a9770b7ebdfb051150972e649644526e` adds the current admission/timing fields needed for the next rows, including the prefill-drain versus generation-loop split.

Current runtime anchors:
- v6e decode-heavy `decode_b32_i1_o128_n4`: `3197.58` Levanter vs `3408.09` vLLM decode tok/s, ratio `0.938`.
- v6e mixed `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1`: `4084.24` Levanter vs `4985.21` vLLM decode tok/s, ratio `0.819`, all `16384` expected completion tokens.
- v6e prefill-heavy `prefill_b8_i2048_o128_n1`: initial ratio `0.797`, corrected backend=both rerun `/dlwh/qwen3-v6e8-prefillcorr-20260607-0023` remained an end-to-end target failure at `0.742`, and post-split rerun `/dlwh/qwen3-v6e8-prefillpostsplit-20260607-0419` remains a target failure at `0.758`. The post-split row shows `1614.816` generation tok/s and only `0.171s` prefill drain in the measured iteration; the remaining decision is tracked in #6229.
- v5p mixed `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1`: TP=8 startup retry failed because vLLM/tpu_inference saw only 4 devices; bounded TP=4 retry `/dlwh/qwen3-mixed-v5p-startupdiag-tp4-i512-o512-20260607-0724` succeeded but is a target failure at `0.600` (`3131.59` Levanter vs `5215.67` vLLM decode tok/s; `6263.19` vs `10431.34` total tok/s), with all `16384` completion tokens produced.

### Definition of Done
- [x] Matrix rows are reproducible from committed benchmark config.
- [x] Each row records backend, shape, throughput, token completion, admission/chunking metrics, and pass/fail target in the harness output.
- [ ] v6e-8 rows cover the core RL rollout regimes with current #6185 timing/admission metrics.
- [ ] v5p rows are produced after the v5p startup issue is understood or bypassed.
- [x] Current anchors are linked from the RL rollout epic and handoff PR.

### Current Next Step
Do not launch matrix runs automatically from this tracker. Once #6185 `f55913d1`/`d63d1edf` lands, or maintainers explicitly authorize reruns from that head, refresh the highest-value v6e rows first: the canonical decode-heavy RL row and the corrected mixed `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1` row. Skip additional prefill-heavy `prefill_b8_i2048_o128_n1` rows unless #6229 explicitly chooses another optimization experiment. Use the new `generation_*` and `prefill_drain_*` fields when interpreting prefill-heavy rows; the collected post-split row shows the generation loop is not the weak point. For v5p, use TP=4 on `v5p-8`; #6230 now has a real mixed row and the remaining question is the `0.600` throughput gap, not startup evidence.

spillover_issues.title: [levanter] Complete dense Qwen3-8B TPU parity matrix

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Description
Track the work to make Levanter TPU inference a reliable RL rollout backend for dense 8B-class models. This narrows the older inference epic #1898 to the current Qwen3-8B TPU rollout line: v6e first, v5p next, correctness under mixed prompt/decode workloads, and token-native RL rollout integration.

Current proof points: PR #6176 carries the dense Qwen3 matrix harness and is green; PR #6185 proves the v6e mixed long-prompt correctness fix, the `0.819` vLLM ratio for `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1`, bounded request logging, vLLM startup log tails, the `f55913d1` prefill-drain/generation timing split, the post-split #6229 row showing `0.758` end-to-end but `1614.816` generation tok/s for `prefill_b8_i2048_o128_n1`, and the `d63d1edf` move of the v6e diagnostic log into `.agents/ops/`; it is terminal green/skipped after one external HF/cache rerun; PR #6214 is the durable handoff, is non-draft/ready for review, and is terminal green/skipped at docs-only head `ebbe9a69d` after clarifying review/landing order and correcting the checked-in current-state head; previous heads `67e9500fc`, `2c43f0d91`, and `dbc3bf595` were also terminal green/skipped; PR #6186 carries the token-native rollout API/data-plane slice and is green; PR #6240 is the ready-for-review v5p startup diagnostics hardening, rebased onto #6185 `d63d1edf`, and is terminal green/skipped after the post-rebase checks, including `levanter-tpu-tests`; the bounded v5p TP=4 retry now proves vLLM can start on `v5p-8` when TP matches the 4 visible devices, but the mixed row is a target failure at `0.600` Levanter/vLLM.

### Definition of Done
- Canonical decode-heavy v6e RL rollout row remains at least `0.90` of vLLM-TPU.
- Mixed long-prompt workloads complete all expected tokens or fail loudly.
- Dense Qwen3-8B matrix is reported by regime with pass/fail status.
- v6e prefill-heavy and v5p failures have tracked follow-ups.
- RL rollout callers can consume token-native outputs with logprobs, masks, and prompt/completion boundaries.

### Subissues
- [x] #6184 - Add multi-prefill admission for long-prompt TPU serving.
- [ ] #6228 - Complete dense Qwen3-8B TPU parity matrix.
- [ ] #6229 - Optimize v6e prefill-heavy decode gap.
- [ ] #6230 - Stabilize v5p Qwen3-8B TPU benchmark startup.
- [ ] #6231 - Finish token-native RL rollout data plane.

### Current Review Order
- #6176: review/land for dense matrix harness and committed benchmark config; green/skipped.
- #6185: review/land as the serving/runtime correctness dependency; green/skipped with v6e mixed runtime proof.
- #6240: review/land after #6185, or keep stacked until #6185 merges; green/skipped diagnostics hardening for future v5p startup failures.
- #6186: review/land after the serving stack is accepted, unless maintainers accept the current stack ordering; green/skipped token-native RL rollout slice.
- #6214: non-draft handoff artifact; not a production-code dependency, green/skipped at `ebbe9a69d`.

### Progress Log
- 2026-06-06: v6e mixed long-prompt correctness and issue-level performance proof landed in PR #6185: all `16384` expected completion tokens, four prefill chunks, one decode iteration, Levanter/vLLM ratio `0.819`.
- 2026-06-06: v6e prefill-heavy comparison found the next gap: `prefill_b8_i2048_o128_n1` at Levanter/vLLM ratio `0.797` (`1006.83` vs `1262.90` decode tok/s; `17116.08` vs `21469.31` total tok/s).
- 2026-06-06: corrected v6e prefill-heavy diagnostic completed at `/dlwh/qwen3-v6e8-prefilldiag-drain-prefill-b8-i2048-o128-n1-20260606-1532`. The clean signal is `1022 / 0.813s` production decode iteration throughput, close to the original vLLM row; the earlier production `decode_submit_seconds` field included prefill-drain work.
- 2026-06-06: PR #6185 reports decode iteration/device throughput and surfaces vLLM startup stderr/stdout tails for future v5p failures.
- 2026-06-06: v5p mixed comparison `/dlwh/qwen3-mixed-v5p-prefilldrain-i512-o512-20260606-0447` failed before benchmark rows because vLLM did not become ready within the startup timeout; this is tracked in #6230 and is not a Levanter throughput result.
- 2026-06-06: PR #6176 (`104bf901`) and PR #6186 (`c4ba37b`) have all visible checks green. #6228 and #6231 track the dense-matrix and token-native data-plane state.
- 2026-06-07: PR #6240 (`32505d1ca`) is ready for review and adds bounded vLLM startup runtime/package/env snapshots for future v5p failures; after rebase onto #6185 `d63d1edf`, it is terminal green/skipped, including `levanter-unit`, `levanter-torch`, `levanter-tpu-tests`, `marin-integration`, `marin-lint`, CodeQL, ReadTheDocs, and the relevant change/unit lanes.
- 2026-06-07: Corrected v6e prefill-heavy backend=both rerun `/dlwh/qwen3-v6e8-prefillcorr-20260607-0023` succeeded from #6185 `91f6ec06a`. End-to-end ratio is still a target failure at `0.742` (`898.94` vs `1212.15` decode tok/s), but corrected fields show Levanter decode iteration at `1200.223` tok/s and device throughput at `1509.350` tok/s; the remaining #6229 target is prefill/host wall-clock overhead, not a proven decode-device regression.
- 2026-06-07: #6185 commit `f7275e5a` removes one concrete #6229 host-overhead source by logging bounded request metadata instead of serializing full long-prompt token lists at INFO. Focused validation passed (`test_inference_server.py`: `19 passed, 1 skipped`, plus pre-commit/Pyrefly on touched files).
- 2026-06-07: #6185 commit `f55913d1` adds the next timing split for #6229: `prefill_drain_seconds_per_iteration`, `prefill_drain_tokens_per_iteration`, `generation_seconds_per_iteration`, `generation_host_seconds_per_iteration`, `generation_tokens_per_iteration`, and derived `generation_tokens_per_second`. This prevents future rows from treating prefill-drain-heavy iterations as pure generation-loop throughput. Validation passed (`test_engine.py` and `test_qwen3_tpu_inference_parity_bench.py`: `63 passed`, plus focused pre-commit/Pyrefly).
- 2026-06-07: #6185 at `f55913d1` is terminal green after one failed-job rerun for the known external Hugging Face/cache-miss class. #6214 at `b44cdc5c9` was terminal green/skipped after the docs-only handoff correction; it records in the checked-in artifact that `0182e9334` was also terminal green/skipped.
- 2026-06-07: #6214 advanced to docs-only head `ebbe9a69d` and is open, non-draft, review-required, and terminal green/skipped, including `marin-integration` (5m4s), `marin-lint`, CodeQL, ReadTheDocs, and the relevant unit/change lanes. This head corrects the checked-in review/landing order and current-state head; previous heads `67e9500fc`, `2c43f0d91`, and `dbc3bf595` were also terminal green/skipped. #6176, #6185, #6186, #6214, and #6240 descriptions link back to #6227 and their child trackers where applicable.
- 2026-06-07: #6231 now documents the PrimeIntellect decision: do not block #6186 on converting `PrimeIntellectEnv` to token-native; keep it OpenAI/verifiers-compatible for this stack while preserving attached response token IDs and tokenizer/policy replay identity, with PrimeIntellect/verifiers token-native work split to follow-ups after #6185/#6186 land.
- 2026-06-07: #6228 now gates dense-matrix reruns on #6185 `f55913d1`/`d63d1edf` landing or explicit maintainer authorization, prioritizes canonical v6e decode/mixed rows plus at most one #6229 prefill-heavy row, and records v5p as no longer gated on startup evidence after the TP=4 mixed row succeeded at `0.600` Levanter/vLLM.
- 2026-06-07: #6185 advanced to docs-only head `d63d1edf`, moving the v6e prefill-heavy diagnostic log from `docs/` to `.agents/ops/2026-06-06-v6e-prefill-diagnostic.md` with ops metadata and a standalone TL;DR. After `marin-integration` and `levanter-unit` hit external Hugging Face/cache failures and each failed lane was rerun once, all visible #6185 checks are green or skipped. No TPU runs or Iris mutations were made.
- 2026-06-07: Authorized reviewer-wait rerun `/dlwh/qwen3-v6e8-prefillpostsplit-20260607-0419` succeeded from #6185 `d63d1edf`. vLLM measured `1264.03` decode tok/s / `21488.50` total; Levanter measured `957.72` decode tok/s / `16281.24` total, ratio `0.758`, target fail. New split fields show generation `0.629s` for `1016` tokens (`1614.816` tok/s), prefill drain `0.171s` for `6` tokens, and generation host `0.006s`; #6229 now needs an optimize-vs-deprioritize decision, not another evidence row.
- 2026-06-07: Bounded v5p TP=4 retry `/dlwh/qwen3-mixed-v5p-startupdiag-tp4-i512-o512-20260607-0724` succeeded from #6240 `32505d1ca` after the TP=8 retry failed on 4 visible devices. vLLM measured `5215.67` decode tok/s / `10431.34` total; Levanter measured `3131.59` decode tok/s / `6263.19` total, ratio `0.600`, target fail. Levanter produced all `16384` completion tokens with four prefill admissions/chunks and `3553.034` generation tok/s; #6230 now tracks the v5p throughput gap rather than startup evidence.

### Related
- Broad inference epic: #1898
- Dense matrix PR: #6176
- Multi-prefill PR: #6185
- Handoff PR: #6214
- Token rollout API PR: #6186
- v5p startup diagnostics PR: #6240

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
🤖 Filed by an agent (`agent-generated`) as a follow-up to the overlay-accessor fix for the split-slice bugs (#2/#3 in the control-plane audit).

## Context

Within a single reconcile batch, the apply pass applies per-`(task, attempt)` updates sequentially against a shared `WorkingState` overlay. Guards that read **raw snapshot** state (instead of the overlay) make the outcome depend on the non-deterministic order workers are processed (`worker_provider` async gather). The immediate split-slice instances are being fixed by adding the missing overlay-aware `WorkingState.attempt_state()` accessor and pointing the ~6 reconcile guards at it (twin of the existing `task_state()` accessor).

That targeted fix removes order-dependence for attempt/task **state** reads (the complete set today), but it relies on **per-guard discipline**: any new guard that reads a raw snapshot field can reintroduce order-dependence. Non-state row fields are already read raw — `failure_count`, `max_retries_failure`, `current_attempt_id` — which a same-batch `TaskRowDelta` could in principle make stale.

## Proposal

Make order-independence **structural** rather than per-guard. Two candidate approaches:

1. **Per-task update coalescing** — collect all updates targeting a given `(task, attempt)` within a batch and resolve them by priority (terminal > requeue > running-repoll) before applying once, so arrival order cannot matter.
2. **Overlay-only invariant** — enforce "no reconcile guard dereferences raw `snapshot.attempts`/`snapshot.tasks` state once an overlay exists" via a lint/assertion, so the per-guard discipline is mechanically guaranteed.

## Acceptance

A property/permutation test that shuffles worker-processing order within a batch and asserts identical final DB state (`deterministic_dump`) across all permutations — the durable regression guard the per-instance fixes don't provide.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read related code in `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/`
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs introducing `WorkingState`)
- [x] Post Research + analysis comment for human review
- [ ] Implementation deferred — design choice (Approach 1 vs 2) requires owner input

# Research

The `WorkingState` overlay this issue presupposes is not on `main`. It is introduced by **PR #5987** (`weaver/iris-reconcile-performance`), which adds `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/working_state.py` along with `task_state()` and a delta accumulator. This issue is a **follow-up to that PR** and is effectively blocked behind it until it lands.

On that branch, the apply pass already uses `state.task_state()` for the in-batch state guards in [`batches.py` `apply_reconcile_batch`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/batches.py#L283) and [`apply_terminal_decisions_batch`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/batches.py#L465). The remaining raw reads are the per-update kernel in [`task.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py#L349) which still pulls `task.failure_count`, `task.preemption_count`, `task.current_attempt_id`, `task.max_retries_failure`/`_preemption` straight off `snapshot.tasks` (lines 349, 392, 445–446, 492, 497). Same for `snapshot.attempts` at line 350 → `attempt.state`, `attempt.finished_at_ms`, `attempt.worker_id` (lines 381, 415–422, 439). Each of these can in principle be made stale within a batch by an earlier `TaskRowDelta`/`AttemptRowDelta`.

Order source: `reconcile_workers_async` gathers worker plans concurrently, so the per-worker arrival order in `plan_results` (the iteration order of the apply loop) is non-deterministic.

**Relevant code (branch `weaver/iris-reconcile-performance`)**
- [`task.py#L349-L350`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py#L349-L350) — raw `snapshot.tasks` / `snapshot.attempts` dereference at top of per-update kernel
- [`task.py#L445-L497`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py#L445-L497) — `failure_count`, `preemption_count`, `max_retries_*` read raw and used for retry-vs-terminal branching
- [`working_state.py#L127-L132`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/working_state.py#L127-L132) — `task_state()` accessor; no `attempt_state` / `task_row` / `attempt_row` counterpart yet
- [`batches.py#L283`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/batches.py#L283) — `apply_reconcile_batch` loop; per-worker iteration order is the order-dependence source

# Analysis of the two proposals

**Approach 1 (per-(task, attempt) coalescing).** As stated this would coalesce duplicate observations for the same `(task, attempt)`. That collision is rare — within one batch each worker emits one observation per attempt, so the realistic order-dependence is **across attempts of the same task or across the task vs its peer-cascade** (`failure_count` accumulation, `current_attempt_id` rotation, sibling requeue races). Coalescing at `(task, attempt)` granularity would not catch the cross-attempt case; coalescing at task granularity would, but loses per-attempt fidelity for the kernel's stale-attempt branch (`update.attempt_id != task.current_attempt_id`). Also: the kernel has side-effects (`record_worker_build_failed`, peer cascade fan-out, recompute work-list) that would need to be split out or proven associative under coalescing. High blast radius.

**Approach 2 (overlay-only invariant).** Add the missing accessors — `WorkingState.task_row(task_id) -> ActiveTaskRow | None` and `WorkingState.attempt_row(task_id, attempt_id) -> AttemptRow | None` — each layering the delta accumulator over the snapshot. Repoint the four raw reads in `task.py` (and the `_apply_single_update` attempt fetch) at the overlay. Then add an AST purity check alongside the existing [`test_reconcile_path_purity.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/tests/cluster/controller/test_reconcile_path_purity.py) that forbids `snapshot.tasks[...]` / `snapshot.attempts[...]` / `.<field>` traversal inside the apply path. Surgical, builds directly on the PR #5987 substrate. Cost is per-field overlay fold extension (`TaskRowDelta` already carries `failure_count`/`preemption_count`; `AttemptRowDelta` already carries `state`/`finished_at`/`error`).

**Recommendation: Approach 2.** Smaller, additive, leans on the AST guard precedent PR #5987 already establishes. The `(task, attempt)` coalescer in Approach 1 is the wrong scope for the actual race, and refactoring the kernel's side-effects to be coalescing-safe is a much larger change than wiring two accessors and a lint.

The **permutation property test** in the Acceptance criterion is approach-independent and should land alongside whichever fix is chosen: shuffle the iteration order of `plan_results` in `apply_reconcile_batch`, materialize via `deterministic_dump`, assert all permutations are equal. The replay-golden harness in [`tests/cluster/controller/replay/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/iris-reconcile-performance/lib/iris/tests/cluster/controller/replay) is the natural host.

# Sequencing

1. Wait for PR #5987 to merge (`WorkingState`, `ControllerEffects`, AST purity guard).
2. Add `task_row()` / `attempt_row()` overlay accessors on `WorkingState`.
3. Repoint `task._apply_single_update` raw dereferences.
4. Extend the AST purity guard with `snapshot.tasks`/`snapshot.attempts` ban inside `apply_*_batch`.
5. Land the permutation test.

Stopping here — choosing Approach 1 vs 2 and the test's host file are decisions for the PR #5987 author. Not opening a PR until that lands.

spillover_issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This sweep investigated recurrent NaNs in `experiments/grug/parallel_attn_mlp` by running a region-pinned v6e-4 learning-rate sweep and then a larger v6e-32 confirmation. The useful result was that the default-style `lr=3e-3, warmup=1000` run stayed finite through 400 steps and beat the `2e-3` run on loss; a v6e-32 confirmation reached step 500 successfully. Further sweep breadth was blocked by repeated Iris launch kills, so the practical conclusion is that the parallel-attn-mlp path had a reproducible non-NaN setting, with infra instability limiting broader hyperparameter exploration.

### Helpful links
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/3316#issuecomment-4010637025
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/3316#issuecomment-4014263360
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description
Parallel-attn-mlp Grug runs on Nemotron mix have shown recurrent `NaN` loss behavior. We need a controlled hyperparameter sweep on `v6e-4` to find stable (non-NaN) settings before scaling back up.

## Hypothesis or Goal
Find at least one reproducible hyperparameter configuration for `experiments/grug/parallel_attn_mlp` that does not enter NaN over an initial stability window.

Success metrics:
- primary: no `NaN` in `train/loss` through at least 400 steps
- secondary: finite eval losses at first eval checkpoint
- tertiary: stable gradient norms (no `NaN` in `grad/norm/total` watch intervals)

Initial hypotheses:
- effective LR schedule is too aggressive for the parallel residual variant
- longer warmup and/or lower peak LR should prevent early numerical failure
- stronger stabilizers (`z_loss_weight`, lower `max_grad_norm`) may help if LR-only tuning is insufficient

First experiment matrix (one-axis first):
- baseline: current parallel config (`lr=3e-3`, `warmup=1000`, `z_loss=1e-4`, `max_grad_norm=1.0`)
- LR sweep (holding other vars fixed): `3e-3`, `2e-3`, `1e-3`, `5e-4`
- then warmup sweep around best LR: `1000`, `2000`, `4000`
- then stabilization sweep if needed: `z_loss_weight` and `max_grad_norm`

Fixed baseline case:
- `experiments/grug/parallel_attn_mlp/launch.py` default optimizer/trainer settings
- run on `v6e-4` so hardware stays constant during the sweep

Stop criteria:
- stop when we get at least one `replicated` non-NaN config (>=2 runs) or when all planned one-axis sweeps fail and we need architecture-level changes.

### Links
- Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/grug_parallel_attn_mlp_v6e4_nan_sweep.md` (to be updated with permalink snapshots)
- W&B project: `marin`

## Results
In progress.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
Aborting a table-spec migration reverts the table to the legacy path but leaves the objects the migration already wrote under `_finelog/tables/<table>/` with no sweeper: `collect_objects` in `store/table/maintenance.rs` returns early when the table is not object-backed, so the aborted table's own GC loop never runs again.

Observed on marin-dev during the #8748 staging validation: aborting `iris.provisioning` at 1,233/1,259 backfilled rows left 3 dereferenced parquet objects (32,732 B), 3 index bundles (85,189 B), 4 catalog revisions, and HEAD.json that the post-abort catalog (generation 4) no longer references. A service restart and a subsequent GC pass (which correctly pruned `zephyr.stage`'s superseded catalogs 35→2) did not touch them. The 24 h orphan grace period had not elapsed at observation time, so re-check `gs://marin-us-central2/finelog/marin-dev/_finelog/tables/iris.provisioning/` after 2026-08-30T23:15Z before treating retention as confirmed.

The retained HEAD is intentional (recovery recognizes the legacy-authority state and a later re-registration reuses the table directory), but the dereferenced data and index objects are bounded garbage per aborted migration. A sweep for tables whose durable state selects the legacy version — or routing them through the store-level orphan GC — would close it.

Part of the object-native storage rollout (#8737, PR #8748).

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Reproduce/locate the reported code path
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs/issues)
- [x] Root-cause analysis
- [x] Decide scope and hand off

The referenced code (`store/table/maintenance.rs`, `collect_objects`, object-backed tables) exists only on the branch of open PR [#8748](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8748) (`agent/20260827-fix-8737`); it is not on `main`. So this is a follow-up to in-flight work, not a `main`-based bug — no parallel PR. Analysis below is for folding into #8748.

**Research**

The GC gate is too strict. [`collect_objects` returns early](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/table/maintenance.rs#L312-L315) when [`is_object_backed()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/table/controller.rs#L207-L211) is false, and that predicate is `object_persistence_configured() && (spec_selects_objects || head_published)`. After an aborted spec migration the active definition reverts to the legacy version, so [`spec_selects_objects` refreshes to false](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/table/controller.rs#L234-L237); the table's own sweep then no-ops even though its `_finelog/tables/<table>/` objects from the migration are still on disk. Both maintenance branches already enqueue [`ObjectCollection`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/table/maintenance.rs#L207-L219), so the plumbing exists — only the predicate blocks the reverted table.

The store-level sweep it would call, [`run_gc_states` → `gc_obsolete_states`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/catalog/object_state_store.rs#L308-L346), only needs `require_objects()` and a resolvable HEAD; it keys off the current HEAD/state, prunes superseded revisions under `state_retention`/`orphan_grace`, and preserves the live HEAD — exactly the intended behavior for the post-abort (generation 4) authority. Note it short-circuits to `Ok(0)` when [`load()` returns `None`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/catalog/object_state_store.rs#L316-L318), and [`load()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/catalog/object_state_store.rs#L54-L94) returns `Some` whenever HEAD validates, independent of legacy-vs-object authority.

**Proposed fix (for #8748)**

Relax the `collect_objects` gate so a table that is object-persistence-configured and still owns residual object state under its directory is swept even when its active spec selects the legacy version — routing it through the existing `run_gc_states`/`gc_obsolete_states` path rather than adding a new sweeper. The fenced-writer guard already in `gc_obsolete_states` stays. Two things to confirm while implementing, since they decide whether relaxing the guard alone is sufficient: (1) whether the abort/recovery path keeps HEAD resolvable so `load()` returns the generation-4 state (if authority-revert makes `load()` return `None`, the store sweep also needs a residual-object path); (2) that pruning respects the intentional HEAD retention on a legacy-authority table. Add a regression test that migrates a table to objects, aborts mid-backfill, runs a maintenance cycle, and asserts dereferenced parquet/index/catalog objects are collected past the grace window while HEAD and the current state survive.

Caveat: the marin-dev observation is still provisional — the 24 h orphan grace had not elapsed, so re-check `gs://marin-us-central2/finelog/marin-dev/_finelog/tables/iris.provisioning/` after 2026-08-30T23:15Z, per the issue, before treating the leak as confirmed rather than merely delayed.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Closing: the mechanism claim here was wrong, and the real defect it led to is now fixed on the PR branch.

The abort does not strand the table's GC. `is_object_backed()` stays true through the retained HEAD (`head_published` latches on the live server and `adopt_claimed` re-latches it on every boot), so the legacy maintenance cycle keeps dispatching `ObjectCollection` for the aborted table. marin-dev confirms it empirically: the three superseded catalog revisions were swept once the 1-hour retention window elapsed (only the current gen-4 catalog, HEAD, and the data/index objects still inside the 24-hour orphan grace remain at `_finelog/tables/iris.provisioning/`).

Writing the regression test for this exposed the genuine bug adjacent to it: the orphan sweep walked only `objects/` and the referenced-key set collected only data-source IDs, so orphaned index bundles and covering-projection artifacts were never collected for any table. Fixed in 7d9b381997 (PR #8748): the reference set now keeps every object a retained state names, the sweep covers `objects/`, `indices/`, and `projections/`, and the test drives register → migrate → abort → GC and verifies only HEAD and the current catalog remain.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
The production `levanter.metrics` namespace carries a catalog segment row for the nested partitioned path `run_id/31/seg_L2_0000000000801962040.parquet` whose file does not exist on disk. Local segment adoption prunes the row's 59 sibling rows but leaves this one (the nested `run_id/31/` path shape appears to escape the reconciliation walk), and the legacy archive uploader then retries the upload every ~30 s forever:

```
WARN finelog::store::legacy::archive: legacy archive upload failed ... No such file or directory
```

Reproduced identically in both full-sample rehearsal rounds for #8748 against a copied production store (31 retries in a ~15 minute window, the only warning category present in an otherwise clean run). Pre-existing on main; unrelated to the object-native branch. Fix likely belongs in adoption's footer-reconciliation walk (treat a catalog row whose path contains partition subdirectories the same as a flat row when the file is absent) plus a retry backoff or tombstone for upload sources that arepermanently missing.

Found during the #8737 / PR #8748 rehearsals.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read the issue and check actionability
- [x] Locate the `finelog::store::legacy::archive` code and the reconciliation walk
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (open PRs / issues)
- [x] Decide scope: analysis comment vs PR

**Not a main-branch fix.** The `store::legacy::archive` module, `adopt_local_segments`, and the nested-partition L1+ layout the report describes exist only on the `agent/20260827-fix-8737` branch of the still-open [PR #8748](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8748); none of it is on `main` (`grep` for `legacy archive` / `store::legacy` across `main` returns nothing). So the "pre-existing on main" framing is off — this is a defect inside the object-native rework itself, and any fix lands on that PR's branch, not against `main`. Per the fix-issue duplicate-work rule I am not opening a parallel implementation PR over an open PR that owns this subsystem.

**Research.** The recurring `No such file or directory` warning is `legacy upload read failed`: archive `sync()` walks every `L>=1` `LOCAL` catalog row and `tokio::fs::read`s the file; a row pointing at an absent file sets `all_durable = false` and is retried on every ~30s sync, forever, with no backoff or tombstone ([archive.rs sync/read](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/legacy/archive.rs#L82-L114)). Adoption pass 1 is supposed to prune exactly this: a `LOCAL` catalog row whose file is gone is dropped via `remove_segment` ([adopt.rs pass 1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/adopt.rs#L641-L657)). Removal keys purely on whether `row.path` is present in `local_files`, and `local_files` comes from a recursive `discover_segments` walk that does descend partition subdirectories ([segment.rs discover](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/segment.rs#L620-L677)) — so a `LOCAL` row with a missing nested file *should* be pruned, which is why the surviving `run_id/31/…` row is surprising.

The most likely escape is a `row.path` string mismatch: `local_files` is keyed by `discover_segments`' `to_string_lossy()` path, and the phantom row survives only if its stored path fails to match that keying (normalization / absolute-vs-relative for the nested partition shape), or if its `location` is `BOTH` rather than `LOCAL` (pass 1 would then collapse it to `REMOTE`, not remove it — yet archive sync only reads `LOCAL` rows, so that alone would not produce the warning). I could not confirm which without the copied production store from the rehearsal.

**Proposed approach (for #8748, two independent defenses):**
1. Reconciliation: make adoption prune a phantom nested-partition `LOCAL` row the same as a flat one. The concrete check is whether the catalog `path` for the `run_id/31/seg_L2_*.parquet` row matches the string `discover_segments` produces for that same physical file — if they diverge, normalize both sides to one canonical form before the `local_files` lookup at [adopt.rs L641-L643](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/adopt.rs#L641-L657). A regression test: seed a catalog `LOCAL` row under `ns/31/seg_L2_*.parquet` with no file on disk, run `adopt_local_segments`, assert the row is removed.
2. Archive sync: give a `LOCAL` upload source whose local read fails `NotFound` a backoff or a tombstone so it stops retrying every 30s, rather than logging forever ([archive.rs L96-L102](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20260827-fix-8737/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/legacy/archive.rs#L96-L102)).

**To confirm root cause**, please share for the surviving `run_id/31/seg_L2_0000000000801962040.parquet` row: its exact catalog `path` string and `location`, and the path string `discover_segments` yields for the sibling flat rows that *were* pruned. That pins whether the fix belongs in reconciliation path-matching, the row's location handling, or both.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Fixed on the #8748 branch in b0928158df. `localize_source` now distinguishes definitive absence (no local file and an archive miss) from transient failure, and a version-0 import drops such a row instead of retrying it: the restated backfill universe stops owing rows nothing holds, the import completes, and the catalog row that feeds the 30-second upload retry loop is deleted. A regression test reproduces the production shape (a `run_id/31/seg_L2_….parquet` LOCAL row with no bytes anywhere) and verifies the import activates with the row gone.

For `levanter.metrics` specifically, the retry noise ends when the table goes through its object-native migration, which removes the phantom row as an unrecoverable source. This closes with PR #8748.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
On cw-rno2a a 1×H100 pod at interactive priority sat `SchedulingGated` for 23 minutes while the batch band held ~500 of 512 GPUs, then failed its job's endpoint deadline. Kueue reported `QuotaReserved (Pending): couldn't assign flavors to pod set main: topology "infiniband" doesn't allow to fit any of 1 pod(s)` — TAS could not fit the pod, and no batch pod was preempted to make room. The `cw-tas` ClusterQueue sets `preemption.withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority`, but quota is deliberately non-binding ("the pressure signal is TAS, not quota" — `lib/iris/scripts/install_kueue.py`), and on the deployed Kueue version TAS lack-of-fit does not appear to trigger within-queue preemption. The install script itself flags TAS-aware preemption as version-sensitive. Net effect: interactive submissions queue behind batch instead of reclaiming, which contradicts the intended band semantics.

A second interaction worsens it: when TAS finally admits, it pins the pod to one hostname via node affinity from its capacity snapshot; a concurrently admitted gang can take that node's GPU first, leaving the pod `Unschedulable` (`1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 64 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity`). Iris correctly returns the task to PENDING, but the fresh attempt re-enters the same non-preempting queue.

Reproduce:
1. Fill a TAS cluster's GPUs with batch-band Iris jobs.
2. Submit a small interactive-band GPU job.
3. Observe it gated indefinitely with the TAS fit message and no preemption events.

Expected: an interactive-band workload preempts batch-band workloads when TAS cannot fit it, per the documented band semantics.

Observed job: `/power/curriculum-rl-r2-cleanup/eval-20260829-200348-power-curriculum-rl-grade-adaptive-76e2` (inference task events show the full sequence). Marin-side mitigation for the resulting eval deaths is in #8769 (startup timeout no longer consumed by queue time).

Done when:
TAS-driven lack-of-fit for a higher-band workload triggers preemption of lower-band pods (validated on the deployed Kueue version, e.g. via the kind smoke), or the ClusterQueue configuration is changed so band priority is enforced through binding quota.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis** (not opening a PR — the fix is version-sensitive and its definition of done requires validation on the deployed Kueue, larger than a self-contained change).

**Root cause.** The `cw-tas` ClusterQueue asks Kueue for priority preemption via [`preemption.withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py#L363-L377), but every resource carries a sentinel [`NON_BINDING_QUOTA`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py#L114-L123) so quota never binds. Kueue's within-queue preemption selects victims by whether reclaiming their *quota* would admit the pending Workload; with non-binding quota there is never quota pressure, so the only blocker is the TAS topology fit — and on the deployed Kueue the TAS assigner reports lack-of-fit without feeding back into preemption. The higher-band Workload gets `QuotaReserved` but no victims, and its pods stay `SchedulingGated`. The install script already [flags this as version-sensitive](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/scripts/install_kueue.py#L51-L54).

The secondary interaction (node-affinity pin from a stale TAS capacity snapshot losing a race to a concurrently-admitted gang → `Unschedulable` → Iris returns the task to PENDING → re-enters the same non-preempting queue) is a consequence of the same missing preemption, not an independent bug.

**Two viable directions (the DoD names both):**

1. **Make TAS lack-of-fit drive preemption.** This depends entirely on the deployed cks-kueue version and its TAS-preemption support; the feature-gate set is [`CKS_KUEUE_FEATURE_GATES`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py#L52-L59) and the coreweave variant pins no chart version (`latest`). First step is to read the running version (`helm list -n kueue-system`, controller image tag) and check upstream Kueue's TAS-preemption support/gate for it. If a newer chart or gate is required, that is a chart upgrade + gate change, validated by extending the kind smoke ([`gpu_gang_smoke.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/tests/e2e/gpu_gang_smoke.py), which has no preemption case today) with a batch-fills-cluster → interactive-preempts scenario.

2. **Enforce band priority through binding quota** on the scarce accelerator resources (`nvidia.com/gpu`, `rdma/ib`) only, leaving cpu/memory/ephemeral-storage non-binding. Binding GPU quota restores the classic, well-supported preemption path (quota pressure → within-queue `LowerPriority` eviction) without waiting on TAS-preemption. The cost is that GPU quota now has to track real capacity, which fights the "autoscaler is the capacity authority, Kueue never rejects on quota" design the comments call out — so it needs the quota kept in sync with scale-group max slices.

**Recommendation before implementation:** confirm the deployed cks-kueue version and whether it supports TAS-driven within-queue preemption (this decides between directions 1 and 2), and confirm the priority values in [`IRIS_PRIORITY_CLASSES`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3a6afc404d5701883bfc4d6fe063505f5e8fc76f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/types.py#L37-L41) (interactive=10 > batch=0) are the intended reclaim ordering. Either path must ship with a preemption case in the kind smoke as the acceptance gate. Marin-side eval mitigation is already tracked in #8769.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖
**Research**

CoreWeave Pulumi pins [cks-kueue 1.4.0](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/coreweave/kueue.py), which contains Kueue 0.18.0; the kind smoke also pins [upstream 0.18.0](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/scripts/install_kueue.py). Kueue classic preemption starts from quota pressure, while Iris gives every covered resource [sentinel non-binding quota](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/kueue_manifests.py), so the interactive Workload reaches TAS as quota-Fit and topology lack-of-fit downgrades it to NoFit without selecting victims. The evidence task confirms attempt 0 was admitted after 23 minutes, then failed on one GPU-full hostname and was requeued; Kueue 0.18.2 added [same-cycle TAS assignment recomputation](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/pull/12521) for topology domains consumed by an earlier evaluation.

**Proposed Fix**

Upgrade both validation paths to Kueue 0.18.3 via cks-kueue 1.5.0 and the upstream 0.18.3 chart, and explicitly require the TAS recomputation gate. Bind GPU and RDMA quota to the accelerator capacity derived from each cluster's checked-in scale-group maxima, leaving host resources non-binding; this makes interactive-versus-batch accelerator pressure enter Kueue's supported priority-preemption path without duplicating placement logic in Iris. Extend the kind smoke with a batch-fills-quota then interactive-preempts case, and validate the rendered CoreWeave chart/config without changing a shared cluster.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 Fix is in #8782. It pins cks-kueue 1.5.0/Kueue 0.18.3, enables same-cycle TAS assignment recomputation, and derives binding GPU/RDMA quota from each CoreWeave cluster configuration so LowerPriority preemption receives quota pressure before TAS victim selection. The final disposable kind run passed both topology gangs and an interactive-over-batch Kueue preemption event. No shared cluster was changed; #8774 remains separate.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Just kicking off: measure whether adaptive environment/problem sampling improves RL training efficiency under a fixed compute budget, versus uniform random sampling.

## Description

We run SkyRL GRPO post-training on a small Qwen policy (0.6B class) over a pool of verifiable, non-agentic environments (math datasets spanning difficulty, plus simple programmatic tasks). Each arm uses the same model, data pool, and budget; only the policy for choosing which environment/problem to roll out next differs.

Arms:

1. Naive sampling: uniform random over the pool (baseline).
2. Modified Thompson sampling: bias toward environments currently yielding reward signal (e.g. per-env reward variance / pass-rate entropy), with decay so the belief tracks policy drift.
3. Pre-graded difficulty (problems graded 0–N easiest→hardest):
   - Naive curriculum: 1/N of budget per level.
   - Adaptive curriculum: train on a level until it stops paying (saturated or not learning), then move.
   - Biased sampling: grades seed an initial belief distribution for the Thompson sampler.

Budget: fixed output-token count per run, falling back to GPU wall-time (64 H100s x fixed hours) if token accounting is impractical. Runs use INTERACTIVE priority on cw-rno2a. The experiment is wired through Marin artifact steps (`marin.rl.skyrl`) so arms are cached and rerunnable; sampler support lands on a MarinSkyRL branch if the pinned trainer lacks the hooks.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Reward-signal-aware sampling concentrates rollouts where the learning signal is, so adaptive arms should reach a given eval score with fewer output tokens than uniform sampling. Quantify the value of each mechanism at fixed budget.

## Status

Kickoff. Wiring the experiment directory and a small smoke run.

Planned milestones, posted as comments:

1. Initial smoke run working end to end.
2. Curriculum/sampling infrastructure wired.
3. Results per sampling arm.
4. Final report on arm efficacy and follow-up recommendations.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

## Conclusion

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Wiring status: the training loop works end to end; the smoke milestone is blocked only on a MarinSkyRL export bug.

What ran: `experiments/post_training/curriculum_rl/` builds a 6-bin graded pool (GSM8K, MATH L1-2/3/4/5, AIME 1983-2024; 10,427 train rows, 756 validation rows), mirrors Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B@c1899de, and runs SkyRL GRPO on 2 nodes of cw-rno2a H100s at interactive priority through `skyrl_step`, with pool/model artifacts cached across attempts. The smoke run completed all 4 GRPO steps over the mixed-env parquet (per-row `env_class`), logging per-environment metrics (train `environment/acc` 0.023 at step 4 — the raw 0.6B policy under a 1024-token cap).

Fixes landed on the branch along the way:

1. MarinSkyRL pin b45a6ed2 crashed at startup (`SKYRL_DEBUG_ARTIFACT_DIR is required`); advanced to d018d672, which contains the upstream fix.
2. The `aime` env asserts `extras["reward_model"]["ground_truth"]` (the gsm8k env reads `reward_spec`); pool rows now carry both columns.
3. The `aime` env verifies with the Minerva `Answer: ...` extraction, not `\boxed{}`; prompts now elicit a final Answer line. Representative ground truths (integers, degrees, fractions, tuples, radicals, polynomials) pass the skyrl-gym contract's two-sided preflight.

Open blocker: at d018d672 the terminal policy export (`cloud.iris.export_hf_checkpoint`) dies with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'` — `skyrl_train/hf_export.py` pulls `skyrl_train.utils`, whose package init imports torch, into the deliberately torch-free launcher env.
